sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第213卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 213
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 213

sentences.zh: 卷第二百一十三

translations.literal: Roll 213
translations.idiomatic: Volume 213

sentences.zh: 【唐紀二十九】 起柔兆攝提格，盡昭陽作噩，凡八年。

translations.literal: 【Tang Records 29】 From Rouzhao Shetige through Zhaoyang Zuoe; eight years in all.
translations.idiomatic: 【Tang Records 29】 From Rouzhao Shetige through Zhaoyang Zuoe—eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸未，更立契丹松漠王李邵固為廣化王，奚饒樂王李魯蘇為奉誠王。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guiwei, the Khitan Prince of Songmo Li Shaogu was reinstalled as Prince of Guanghua, and the Xi Prince of Raole Li Lusu as Prince of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guiwei, the Khitan Prince of Songmo Li Shaogu was reinstalled as Prince of Guanghua, and the Xi Prince of Raole Li Lusu as Prince of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 以上從甥陳氏為東華公主，妻邵固；

translations.literal: The emperor's senior nephew by marriage, Lady Chen, was made Princess Donghua and given in marriage to Shaogu;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ennobled his senior nephew's wife, Lady Chen, as Princess Donghua and gave her to Shaogu in marriage;

sentences.zh: 以成安公主之女韋氏為東光公主，妻魯蘇。

translations.literal: the daughter of Princess Cheng'an, the Wei clan, was made Princess Dongguang and given in marriage to Lusu.
translations.idiomatic: and he made the daughter of Princess Cheng'an, Lady Wei, Princess Dongguang and gave her to Lusu in marriage.

sentences.zh: 張說奏：「今之五禮，貞觀、顯慶兩曾修纂，前後頗有不同，其中或未折衷。

translations.literal: Zhang Shuo memorialized: "The present Five Rites were twice compiled, in the Zhenguan and Xianqing reigns; before and after they differ considerably, and in some matters may not have been reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shuo submitted a memorial: "The present Five Rites were compiled twice, under Zhenguan and Xianqing, and the two versions differ in many places; some provisions may never have been harmonized.

sentences.zh: 望與學士等討論古今，刪改施行。」

translations.literal: I hope to discuss past and present with the academicians and others, revise and delete, and put them into practice."
translations.idiomatic: I ask permission to discuss them with the academicians, revise the text in light of antiquity and the present, and put a unified version into effect."

sentences.zh: 制從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 邕州封陵獠梁大海等據賓、橫州反；

translations.literal: The Fengling Liao of Yongzhou, Liang Dahai and others, seized Bin and Heng prefectures and rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Dahai of the Fengling Liao in Yongzhou and others seized Bin and Heng prefectures and rose in rebellion;

sentences.zh: 二月，己酉，遣內侍楊思勖發兵討之。

translations.literal: in the second month, on jiyou, the palace attendant Yang Sixu was sent to raise troops and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: in the second month, on jiyou, the emperor sent the palace attendant Yang Sixu at the head of an army to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 上召河南尹崔隱甫，欲用之，中書令張說薄其無文，奏擬金吾大將軍；

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Cui Yinpu, Intendant of Henan, intending to employ him; Chief Minister Zhang Shuo looked down on him for lack of literary polish and memorialized proposing him as General of the Golden Guard;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Cui Yinpu, Intendant of Henan, intending to promote him, but Chief Minister Zhang Shuo, who thought him uncultivated, proposed instead that he be made General of the Golden Guard;

sentences.zh: 前殿中監崔日知素與說善，說薦為御史大夫；

translations.literal: the former Director of the Palace Secretariat Cui Rizhi had long been on good terms with Shuo, and Shuo recommended him as Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: the former Director of the Palace Secretariat Cui Rizhi was an old friend of Shuo's, and Shuo recommended him for Censor-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: the emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以日知為左羽林大將軍，丁巳，以隱甫為御史大夫。

translations.literal: On bingchen Rizhi was made Left General of the Feathered Forest, and on dingsi Yinpu was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Cui Rizhi was appointed Left General of the Feathered Forest; on dingsi Cui Yinpu was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 隱甫由是與說有隙。

translations.literal: Yinpu thereby came to bear a grudge against Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: From this Yinpu and Shuo were at odds.

sentences.zh: 說有才智而好賄，百官白事有不合者，好面折之，至於叱罵。

translations.literal: Shuo was talented and clever but fond of bribes; when officials reported matters with which he disagreed, he liked to rebuke them to their faces, even to the point of shouting abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was clever but greedy for bribes; when an official's report displeased him, he would openly humiliate him, sometimes shouting him down.

sentences.zh: 惡御史中丞宇文融之為人，且患其權重，融所建白，多抑之。

translations.literal: He detested the character of Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong and also feared his great power; proposals Rong submitted were mostly suppressed by him.
translations.idiomatic: He disliked Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong personally and resented his influence; most of Rong's proposals he blocked.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人張九齡言於說曰：「宇文融承恩用事，辯給多權數，不可不備。」

translations.literal: Zhongshu Sheren Zhang Jiuling said to Shuo: "Yuwen Rong, enjoying imperial favor and wielding power, is eloquent and full of stratagems; he must not go unguarded against."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu Sheren Zhang Jiuling told Shuo, "Yuwen Rong enjoys the emperor's favor and is in power; he is quick-tongued and full of schemes—you cannot be too careful."

sentences.zh: 說曰：「鼠輩何能為！」

translations.literal: Shuo said: "What can such rats accomplish!"
translations.idiomatic: Shuo replied, "What can vermin like that do!"

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬子，隱甫、融及御史中丞李林甫共奏彈說「引術士占星，徇私僭侈，受納賄賂。」

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renzi, Yinpu, Rong, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Linfu jointly memorialized impeaching Shuo: "He employed occultists to practice astrology, showed favoritism and presumptuous extravagance, and accepted bribes."
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on renzi, Yinpu, Rong, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Linfu jointly impeached Shuo, charging that "he employed occultists to practice astrology, showed favoritism and lived beyond his rank, and took bribes."

sentences.zh: 敕源乾曜及刑部尚書韋抗、大理少卿明珪與隱甫等同於御史台鞫之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuan Qianyao, Minister of Justice Wei Kang, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Ming Gui, and Yinpu and the others to interrogate him jointly at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yuan Qianyao, Minister of Justice Wei Kang, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Ming Gui, and Yinpu and the rest to try the case together at the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 林甫，叔良之曾孫；

translations.literal: Linfu was the great-grandson of Shuliang;
translations.idiomatic: Linfu was a great-grandson of Li Shuliang;

sentences.zh: 抗，安石之從父兄子也。

translations.literal: Kang was a son of Anshi's father's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was a cousin of Wei Anshi on his father's side.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以戶部侍郎李元紘為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On dingsi Li Yuanhong, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Li Yuanhong, Vice Minister of Revenue, was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 元紘以清儉著，故上用為相。

translations.literal: Yuanhong was known for integrity and frugality, and for this reason the emperor employed him as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong was famed for integrity and frugality, which was why the emperor made him a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 源乾曜等鞫張說，事頗有狀，上使高力士視說，力士還奏：「說蓬首垢面，席蒿，食以瓦器，惶懼待罪。」

translations.literal: Yuan Qianyao and the others interrogated Zhang Shuo, and the case largely stood proved; the emperor sent Gao Lishi to observe Shuo. Lishi returned and reported: "Shuo's hair is disheveled and his face filthy; he sleeps on straw and eats from earthenware, fearful and awaiting punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianyao and the others tried Zhang Shuo, and the charges largely held; the emperor sent Gao Lishi to see him. Lishi reported back, "Shuo's hair is unkempt and his face dirty; he sleeps on straw and eats from pottery bowls, terrified and waiting to be punished."

sentences.zh: 上意憐之。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart was moved to pity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 力士因言說有功於國，上以為然。

translations.literal: Lishi then said that Shuo had rendered great service to the state, and the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi added that Shuo had served the state well, and the emperor thought this true.

sentences.zh: 庚申，但罷說中書令，餘如故。

translations.literal: On gengshen only Shuo's post as Chief Minister was removed; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the emperor merely removed Shuo from the post of Chief Minister; his other offices were left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，太子太傅岐王范薨，贈謚惠文太子。

translations.literal: On dingmao the Prince of Qi, Fan, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, died; he was posthumously given the title Prince Huiwen.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the Prince of Qi, Fan, who was Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, died and was posthumously honored as Prince Huiwen.

sentences.zh: 上為之撤膳累旬，百官上表固請，然後復常。

translations.literal: For him the emperor abstained from meals for many days; only after the hundred officials submitted memorials earnestly pleading did he return to his usual fare.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went without regular meals for many days in mourning; only after officials repeatedly memorialized did he resume his normal diet.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，太原尹張孝嵩奏：「有李子嶠者，自稱皇子，雲生於潞州，母曰趙妃。」

translations.literal: On dinghai Zhang Xiaosong, Intendant of Taiyuan, memorialized: "There is one Li Ziqiao who calls himself an imperial prince, saying he was born in Luzhou and that his mother was Consort Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Zhang Xiaosong, Intendant of Taiyuan, reported that "a man named Li Ziqiao claims to be an imperial prince, saying he was born in Luzhou and that his mother was Consort Zhao."

sentences.zh: 上命杖殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，於定、恆、莫、易、滄五州置軍以備突厥。

translations.literal: On xinchou armies were established in the five prefectures of Ding, Heng, Mo, Yi, and Cang to guard against the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou garrisons were set up in Ding, Heng, Mo, Yi, and Cang prefectures to guard against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 上欲以武惠妃為皇后，或上言：「武氏乃不戴天之仇，豈可以為國母！

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Consort Wu Huifei empress; someone remonstrated with the throne: "The Wu clan is an enemy with whom one cannot live under the same sky—how can she become mother of the state!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make Consort Wu Huifei empress, but someone warned him, "The Wu are your family's mortal enemies—how can a Wu become empress and mother of the realm!

sentences.zh: 人間盛言張說欲取立後之功，更圖入相之計。

translations.literal: Among the people it was widely said that Zhang Shuo sought merit in establishing her as empress and further plotted a plan to reenter the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor had it that Zhang Shuo hoped to win credit by helping install her and then regain the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 且太子非惠妃所生，惠妃復自有子，若登宸極，太子必危。」

translations.literal: Moreover the Heir Apparent was not born of Consort Huifei, and Huifei again had sons of her own; if she ascended the imperial seat, the Heir Apparent would surely be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the crown prince is not her son, and she has sons of her own; if she becomes empress, the heir will be in grave danger."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 然宮中禮秩，一如皇后。

translations.literal: Yet within the palace her ritual rank was the same as an empress.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace, however, she was treated with the ceremonial standing of an empress.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸卯，戶部奏今歲戶七百六萬九千五百六十五，口四千一百四十一萬九千七百一十二。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guimao, the Ministry of Revenue reported that this year there were 7,069,565 households and 41,419,712 persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guimao, the Ministry of Revenue reported 7,069,565 households and a population of 41,419,712 for the year.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，河南、北大水，溺死者以千計。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Henan and Hebei suffered great floods; those drowned numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Henan and Hebei were struck by severe flooding; thousands drowned.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙午朔，魏州言河溢。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day bingwu, Weizhou reported that the Yellow River had overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month, bingwu, Weizhou reported that the Yellow River had burst its banks.

sentences.zh: 九月，己丑，以安西副大都護、磧西節度使杜暹同平章事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jichou, Du Xian, Vice Protector-General of Anxi and Military Commissioner of Qixi, was made Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jichou, Du Xian, Vice Protector-General of Anxi and Military Commissioner of Qixi, was appointed Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 自王孝傑克復四鎮，復於龜茲置安西都護府，以唐兵三萬戍之，百姓苦其役；

translations.literal: Since Wang Xiaojie recovered the Four Garrisons, the Protectorate-General of Anxi was again established at Kucha, garrisoned by thirty thousand Tang troops; the common people suffered bitterly under the corvée;
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Xiaojie recovered the Four Garrisons, the Anxi Protectorate was re-established at Kucha and garrisoned with thirty thousand Tang troops; the people groaned under the burden of service;

sentences.zh: 為都護者，惟田揚名、郭元振、張嵩及暹皆有善政，為人所稱。

translations.literal: of those who served as Protector-General, only Tian Yangming, Guo Yuanzhen, Zhang Song, and Xian all had good government and were praised by men.
translations.idiomatic: among the protectors-general, only Tian Yangming, Guo Yuanzhen, Zhang Song, and Xian governed well and won public praise.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚申，上幸汝州廣成湯；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on gengshen, the emperor visited the Guangcheng hot springs in Ruzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on gengshen, the emperor visited the Guangcheng hot springs in Ruzhou;

sentences.zh: 己酉，還宮。

translations.literal: on jiyou he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on jiyou he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁巳，上幸壽安，獵於方秀川；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dingsi, the emperor visited Shou'an and hunted at Fangxiu Stream;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingsi, the emperor went to Shou'an and hunted on the Fangxiu River;

sentences.zh: 壬戌，還宮。

translations.literal: on renxu he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on renxu he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 楊思勖討反獠，生擒梁大海等三千餘人，斬首二萬級而還。

translations.literal: Yang Sixu suppressed the rebel Liao, took Liang Dahai and more than three thousand others alive, and beheaded twenty thousand before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sixu put down the rebel Liao, captured Liang Dahai and more than three thousand others alive, took twenty thousand heads, and returned.

sentences.zh: 是歲，黑水靺鞨遣使入見，上以其國內黑水州，仍為置長史以鎮之。

translations.literal: That year the Heishui Mohe sent envoys to court; the emperor, because their state lay within Heishui Circuit, also established a chief administrator to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Heishui Mohe sent envoys to court; because their territory lay within Heishui Circuit, the emperor also appointed a chief administrator to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 勃海靺鞨王武藝曰：「黑水入唐，道由我境。

translations.literal: Wuyi, king of the Bohai Mohe, said: "The Heishui come to Tang by a road through my territory.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi, king of the Bohai Mohe, said, "The Heishui reach Tang only by a road through my lands.

sentences.zh: 往者請吐屯於突厥，先告我與我偕行；

translations.literal: Formerly, when they asked Tutan of the Turks for troops, they first informed me and went together with me;
translations.idiomatic: When they once asked the Turks for Tutan, they told me first and we went together;

sentences.zh: 今不告我而請吏於唐，是必與唐合謀，欲腹背攻我也。」

translations.literal: now without informing me they ask Tang for officials—this must mean they are in league with Tang and intend to attack me from front and rear."
translations.idiomatic: now they ask Tang for officials without telling me—they must be plotting with Tang to strike me from both sides."

sentences.zh: 遣其母弟門藝與其舅任雅將兵擊黑水。

translations.literal: He sent his younger brother by the same mother, Men Yi, and his maternal uncle Ren Ya to lead troops against the Heishui.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his younger uterine brother Men Yi and his maternal uncle Ren Ya to attack the Heishui with an army.

sentences.zh: 門藝嘗為質子於唐，諫曰：「黑水請吏於唐，而我以其故擊之，是叛唐也。

translations.literal: Men Yi had once served as hostage at Tang and remonstrated: "The Heishui ask Tang for officials, yet I attack them for that reason—this is rebellion against Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Men Yi had once been a hostage at the Tang court and objected, "The Heishui asked Tang for officials; if we attack them for that, we rebel against Tang.

sentences.zh: 唐，大國也。

translations.literal: Tang is a great state.
translations.idiomatic: Tang is a great power.

sentences.zh: 昔高麗全盛之時，強兵三十餘萬，不遵唐命，掃地無遺。

translations.literal: In former times when Goguryeo was at its height, with more than three hundred thousand strong troops, it did not obey Tang's commands and was swept clean, leaving nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Goguryeo was at its height it fielded more than three hundred thousand men, yet defying Tang it was utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 況我兵不及高麗什之一二，一旦與唐為怨，此亡國之勢也。」

translations.literal: Moreover our troops do not reach one or two tenths of Goguryeo's; once we incur Tang's enmity, this is the posture of a state on the verge of ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Our forces are not even a tenth or a twentieth of theirs; if we make an enemy of Tang overnight, that is the path to national ruin."

sentences.zh: 武藝不從，強遣之。

translations.literal: Wuyi would not listen and forcibly sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi refused to listen and sent him anyway.

sentences.zh: 門藝至境上，復以書力諫。

translations.literal: When Men Yi reached the border, he again wrote a letter earnestly remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: At the frontier Men Yi wrote again, urging him strongly to desist.

sentences.zh: 武藝怒，遣其從兄大壹夏代之將兵，召，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Wuyi was enraged, sent his elder clansman Dayi to replace him in command of the army, summoned him, and intended to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi flew into a rage, sent his elder clansman Dayi to take command in his place, summoned Men Yi back, and meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 門藝棄眾，間道來奔，制以為左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Men Yi abandoned his troops, came fleeing by a secret route, and was appointed by edict Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Men Yi abandoned his army, slipped away by a hidden path to surrender, and was appointed Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 武藝遣使上表罪狀門藝，請殺之。

translations.literal: Wuyi sent envoys with a memorial listing Men Yi's crimes and asking that he be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi sent envoys memorializing Men Yi's crimes and demanding his execution.

sentences.zh: 上密遣門藝詣安西；

translations.literal: The emperor secretly sent Men Yi to Anxi;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly sent Men Yi to Anxi;

sentences.zh: 留其使者，別遣報雲已流門藝於嶺南。

translations.literal: detained his envoys, and separately sent word reporting that Men Yi had been banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: detained Wuyi's envoys and sent a separate reply saying Men Yi had been exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 武藝知之，上表稱：「大國當示人以信，豈得為此欺誑？」

translations.literal: Wuyi learned of it and memorialized: "A great state ought to show men good faith—how can it practice such deception?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wuyi found out, he memorialized, "A great state should show good faith to the world—how can you deceive us like this?"

sentences.zh: 固請殺門藝。

translations.literal: He firmly asked that Men Yi be killed.
translations.idiomatic: He again demanded Men Yi's death.

sentences.zh: 上以鴻臚少卿李道邃、源復不能督察官屬，致有漏洩，皆坐左遷。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial Li Daosui and Yuan Fu could not supervise their subordinates and allowed a leak, punished both with demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial Li Daosui and Yuan Fu for failing to control their staff and allowing the secret to leak; both were demoted.

sentences.zh: 暫遣門藝詣嶺南以報之。

translations.literal: Men Yi was temporarily sent to Lingnan to report back to him.
translations.idiomatic: Men Yi was briefly sent toward Lingnan so the court could report this to Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：王者所以服四夷，威信而已。

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: What enables a true king to bring the four barbarians to submission is authority and good faith alone.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: A true king subdues the four barbarians by authority and good faith alone.

sentences.zh: 門藝以忠獲罪，自歸天子。

translations.literal: Men Yi, punished for loyalty, came of himself to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Men Yi was punished for loyalty and came to surrender to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 天子當察其枉直，賞門藝而罰武藝，為政之體也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ought to examine right and wrong, reward Men Yi and punish Wuyi—this is the substance of government.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor should weigh right and wrong, reward Men Yi and punish Wuyi—that is how government ought to work.

sentences.zh: 縱不能討，猶當正以門藝之無罪告之。

translations.literal: Even if he could not punish Wuyi, he should still have declared to him that Men Yi was innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he could not punish Wuyi, he should at least have told him plainly that Men Yi was innocent.

sentences.zh: 今明皇威不能服武藝，恩不能庇門藝，顧效小人為欺誑之語，以取困於小國，乃罪鴻臚之漏洩，不亦可羞哉！

translations.literal: Now Emperor Ming's authority could not subdue Wuyi, his grace could not shelter Men Yi; he only imitated petty men in words of deception, thereby finding himself embarrassed before a small state, and then blamed the Court of State Ceremonial for the leak—is this not shameful!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Ming's might could not cow Wuyi, nor his favor protect Men Yi; he stooped to petty deceit and was put in the wrong by a small kingdom, then blamed the Court of State Ceremonial for the leak—how shameful!

sentences.zh: 杜暹為安西都護，突騎施金河公主遣牙官以馬千匹詣安西互市。

translations.literal: When Du Xian was Protector-General of Anxi, the Turgesh Jinhe Princess sent a yamen officer with a thousand horses to Anxi for trade.
translations.idiomatic: While Du Xian was Protector-General of Anxi, the Turgesh Jinhe Princess sent an officer with a thousand horses to trade at Anxi.

sentences.zh: 使者宣公主教，暹怒曰：「阿史那女何得宣教於我？」

translations.literal: The envoy proclaimed the princess's command; Xian angrily said: "How dare a daughter of the Ashina clan issue commands to me?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy announced the princess's orders; Xian flew into a rage: "What right has an Ashina woman to give me orders?"

sentences.zh: 杖其使者，留不遣；

translations.literal: He had the envoy flogged and detained him without sending him back;
translations.idiomatic: He had the envoy beaten and detained;

sentences.zh: 馬經雪死盡。

translations.literal: the horses, passing through snow, all perished.
translations.idiomatic: the horses died in the snow to the last one.

sentences.zh: 突騎施可汗蘇祿大怒，發兵寇四鎮。

translations.literal: The Turgesh qaghan Suolu was greatly enraged and sent troops to raid the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Turgesh Qaghan Suolu was furious and marched against the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 會暹入朝，趙頤貞代為安西都護，嬰城自守；

translations.literal: It happened that Xian entered court; Zhao Yizhen replaced him as Protector-General of Anxi and shut himself in the cities to defend them;
translations.idiomatic: When Xian went to court, Zhao Yizhen took over as Protector-General of Anxi and held the cities under siege;

sentences.zh: 四鎮人畜儲積，皆為蘇祿所掠，安西僅存。

translations.literal: the people, livestock, and stores of the Four Garrisons were all plundered by Suolu; Anxi barely survived.
translations.idiomatic: Suolu looted the people, livestock, and stores of the Four Garrisons; only Anxi itself barely held on.

sentences.zh: 既而蘇祿聞暹入相，稍引退，尋遣使入貢。

translations.literal: Before long Suolu heard that Xian had entered the chief ministership, gradually drew back, and soon sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Suolu learned Xian had become chief minister, he gradually withdrew and soon sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑，涼州都督王君𡙟破吐蕃於青海之西。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinchou, Wang Jun, Military Governor of Liangzhou, defeated the Tibetans west of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinchou, Wang Jun, Military Governor of Liangzhou, defeated the Tibetans west of Qinghai Lake.

sentences.zh: 初，吐蕃自恃其強，致書用敵國禮，辭指悖慢，上意常怒之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Tibetans, relying on their strength, sent letters using the protocol of equal states; the wording was insolent and disrespectful, and the emperor's mind was often angered.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Tibetans, confident in their power, had addressed the court as an equal power in insulting terms, and the emperor was often furious.

sentences.zh: 返自東封，張說言於上曰：「吐蕃無禮，誠宜誅夷，但連兵十餘年，甘、涼、河、鄯、不勝其弊，雖師屢捷，所得不償所亡。

translations.literal: Returning from the eastern feng and shan rites, Zhang Shuo said to the emperor: "The Tibetans are without propriety and truly ought to be punished and destroyed, but for more than ten years armies have been engaged; Gan, Liang, He, and Shan prefectures cannot bear the harm. Though our forces have often been victorious, what is gained does not repay what is lost.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from the eastern feng and shan rites, Zhang Shuo told the emperor, "The Tibetans deserve punishment, but war has dragged on for more than ten years; Gan, Liang, He, and Shan cannot endure the strain. Though we often win battles, the gains do not cover the losses.

sentences.zh: 聞其悔過求和，願聽其款服，以紓邊人。」

translations.literal: I hear they repent their faults and seek peace; I wish to heed their sincere submission to relieve the border people."
translations.idiomatic: I hear they now repent and seek peace; let us accept their submission and give the border people relief."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「俟吾與王君𡙟議之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wait until I discuss it with Wang Jun."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Let me discuss it with Wang Jun first."

sentences.zh: 說退，謂源乾曜曰：「君𡙟勇而無謀，常思僥倖，若二國和親，何以為功！

translations.literal: Shuo withdrew and said to Yuan Qianyao: "Jun is brave but without strategy, always thinking of lucky chances; if the two states make peace by marriage alliance, how will he win merit!
translations.idiomatic: When Shuo withdrew he told Yuan Qianyao, "Jun is brave but rash and always chasing lucky breaks; if Tang and Tibet make peace, how will he win glory!

sentences.zh: 吾言必不用矣。」

translations.literal: My words will surely not be adopted."
translations.idiomatic: My advice will never be taken."

sentences.zh: 及君𡙟入朝，果請深入討之。

translations.literal: When Jun entered court, he indeed asked to campaign deep into their territory to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun came to court, he duly asked for a deep punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 去冬，吐蕃大將悉諾邏寇大斗谷，進攻甘州，焚掠而去。

translations.literal: Last winter the Tibetan general Xinuo-luo raided Dadou Valley, advanced to attack Ganzhou, burned and plundered, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The previous winter the Tibetan general Xinuo-luo raided Dadou Valley, pressed on to Ganzhou, burned and looted, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 君𡙟度其兵疲，勒兵躡其後。

translations.literal: Jun judged their troops weary and led his army in pursuit behind them.
translations.idiomatic: Jun judged the enemy exhausted and led his troops in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，虜凍死者甚眾，自積石軍西歸。

translations.literal: Heavy snow came; very many of the barbarians froze to death, and they returned west from Jishi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell; many of the Tibetans froze to death as they retreated west from Jishi.

sentences.zh: 君𡙟先遣人間道入虜境，燒道旁草。

translations.literal: Jun had earlier sent men by secret routes into barbarian territory to burn the grass along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had already sent men by hidden paths into Tibetan territory to burn the grass along their line of march.

sentences.zh: 悉諾邏至大非川，欲休士馬，而野草皆盡，馬死過半。

translations.literal: When Xinuo-luo reached the Dafei River he wished to rest troops and horses, but the wild grass was all gone and more than half the horses died.
translations.idiomatic: When Xinuo-luo reached the Dafei River and tried to rest men and horses, the pasture was gone and more than half his horses perished.

sentences.zh: 君𡙟與秦州都督張景順追之，及於青海之西，乘冰而度。

translations.literal: Jun and Zhang Jingshun, Military Governor of Qinzhou, pursued them, caught up west of Qinghai, and crossed on the ice.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Zhang Jingshun, Military Governor of Qinzhou, pursued them to the west of Qinghai and crossed on the ice.

sentences.zh: 悉諾邏已去，破其後軍，獲其輜重羊馬萬計而還。

translations.literal: Xinuo-luo had already gone; they smashed his rear guard, seized his baggage train and tens of thousands of sheep and horses, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xinuo-luo had already fled; they routed his rearguard, captured vast baggage, sheep, and horses, and returned.

sentences.zh: 君𡙟以功遷左羽林大將軍，拜其父壽為少府監致仕。

translations.literal: For his merit Jun was transferred to Left General of the Feathered Forest; his father Shou was appointed Director of the Palace Workshops with permission to retire.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat Jun was promoted to Left General of the Feathered Forest, and his father Shou was appointed Director of the Palace Workshops with permission to retire.

sentences.zh: 上由是益事邊功。

translations.literal: The emperor from this increasingly devoted himself to frontier achievements.
translations.idiomatic: From this the emperor devoted himself all the more to frontier glory.

sentences.zh: 初，洛陽人劉宗器上言，請塞汜水舊汴口，更於熒澤引河入汴；

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Zongqi of Luoyang memorialized, asking to block the old Bian mouth at Sishui and instead draw the river into the Bian Canal from Ying Marsh;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a Luoyan named Liu Zongqi had memorialized asking to close the old Bian intake at Sishui and divert the Yellow River into the Bian Canal from Ying Marsh instead;

sentences.zh: 擢宗器為左衛率府冑曹。

translations.literal: Zongqi was promoted to Armorers Clerk in the Left Guards Commandant's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqi was promoted to a post in the Left Guards Commandant's Office.

sentences.zh: 至是，新渠填塞不通，貶宗器為循州安懷戍主。

translations.literal: At this time the new canal silted up and would not pass; Zongqi was demoted to garrison commander of Anhuai in Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By now the new channel had silted shut; Zongqi was demoted to command the Anhuai garrison in Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 命將作大匠范安及發河南、懷、鄭、汴、滑、衛三萬人疏舊渠，旬日而畢。

translations.literal: The Master of Works Fan Anji was ordered to mobilize thirty thousand men from Henan, Huai, Zheng, Bian, Hua, and Wei to dredge the old canal; in ten days it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Master of Works Fan Anji to mobilize thirty thousand laborers from six circuits to dredge the old canal; the work was finished in ten days.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫崔隱甫、中丞宇文融，恐右丞相張說復用，數奏毀之，各為朋黨。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Cui Yinpu and Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong, fearing that Right Chief Minister Zhang Shuo would be employed again, repeatedly memorialized to slander him; each formed a faction.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Cui Yinpu and Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong, fearing Zhang Shuo's return to power, repeatedly denounced him in memorials and each built a faction.

sentences.zh: 上惡之，二月，乙巳，制說致仕，隱甫免官侍母，融出為魏州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor detested this; in the second month, on yisi, an edict made Shuo retire, relieved Yinpu of office to attend his mother, and sent Rong out as Prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loathed this; in the second month, on yisi, he ordered Shuo to retire, let Yinpu leave office to care for his mother, and sent Rong out as prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，制：「諸州逃戶，先經勸農使括定按比後復有逃來者，隨到准白丁例輸當年租庸，有征役得先差。」

translations.literal: On yimao an edict stated: "Fugitive households in the prefectures who, after having been registered and assessed by the agricultural commissioner, flee and return again shall, upon arrival, pay that year's land tax and corvée labor on the standard adult-male basis, and may be drafted first for military service."
translations.idiomatic: “On yimao an edict declared that fugitive households who returned after earlier registration must pay that year's taxes and corvée on the usual adult-male scale and could be drafted first for military service.”

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，癸酉，上悉以諸子慶王潭等領州牧、刺史、都督、節度大使、大都護、經略使，實不出外。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on guiyou, the emperor had all his sons, including Prince Qing Tan and the others, hold the titles of prefect, military governor, commissioner, grand protector-general, and frontier commissioner, but in fact none went out.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on guiyou, the emperor gave all his sons—including Prince Qing Tan—nominal posts as prefects, military governors, commissioners, and frontier protectors, though none actually left court.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗愛晉王，不使出閣；

translations.literal: Earlier Emperor Taizong loved the Prince of Jin and would not let him leave the palace compound;
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning Emperor Taizong loved the Prince of Jin and kept him from leaving the inner palace;

sentences.zh: 豫王亦以武後少子不出閣，及自皇嗣為相王，始出閣。

translations.literal: the Prince of Yu likewise, as Empress Wu's youngest son, did not leave the compound until, from heir apparent he became Prince of Xiang, and only then left the compound.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Yu, as Empress Wu's youngest son, likewise stayed inside until he left the heir's position to become Prince of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 中宗之世，譙王以失愛，謫居外州；

translations.literal: in the age of Emperor Zhongzong the Prince of Qiao, having lost favor, was banished to live in an outer prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhongzong the Prince of Qiao, having fallen from favor, was banished to an outer prefecture;

sentences.zh: 溫王年十七，猶居禁中。

translations.literal: the Prince of Wen at seventeen still lived within the forbidden quarters.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Wen at seventeen still lived inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 上即位，附苑城為十王宅，以居皇子，宦官押之，就夾城參起居，自是不復出閣；

translations.literal: When the present emperor took the throne, he attached the park city to form the Ten Princes' Residence to house the imperial sons; eunuchs guarded them, and through the walled passage they attended to inquire after the emperor's well-being—from this they no longer left the compound;
translations.idiomatic: When the present emperor came to the throne he built the Ten Princes' Residence in the park city for his sons; eunuchs guarded them, and they greeted the emperor through a walled passage—after that they never left the compound again;

sentences.zh: 雖開府置官屬及領籓鎮，惟侍讀時入授書，自餘王府官屬，但歲時通名起居；

translations.literal: although they opened offices, appointed staff, and held nominal frontier commands, only tutors entered at times to teach books; the rest of the princely household staff merely sent their names at the seasons to inquire after well-being;
translations.idiomatic: though they had nominal offices and frontier commands, only tutors entered to teach them; other princely staff merely sent seasonal greetings;

sentences.zh: 其籓鎮官屬，亦不通名。

translations.literal: their frontier-command staff likewise did not send their names.
translations.idiomatic: their frontier staffs did not even send greetings.

sentences.zh: 及諸孫浸多，不置百孫院。

translations.literal: As grandsons gradually multiplied, no Hundred Grandsons' Court was established.
translations.idiomatic: As grandsons grew numerous, no separate residence was set up for them.

sentences.zh: 太子亦不居東宮，常在乘輿所幸之別院。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent likewise did not dwell in the Eastern Palace but constantly stayed in whatever separate residence the imperial carriage favored.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince too did not live in the Eastern Palace but stayed in whatever lodge the emperor favored.

sentences.zh: 上命妃嬪以下宮中育蠶，欲使之知女功。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered consorts and below to raise silkworms within the palace, wishing them to know women's work.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered palace women down to the consorts to raise silkworms, so they would learn women's crafts.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，夏至，賜貴近絲，人一綟。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the summer solstice, silk was bestowed on the honored and near; each person received one bundle.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the summer solstice, the emperor gave silk to his close attendants, one bundle each.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊寅，冀州河溢。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuyin, the Yellow River overflowed in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuyin, the Yellow River flooded Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 己卯，禮部尚書許文憲公蘇頲薨。

translations.literal: On jimao Su Ting, Duke of Xuwenxian, Minister of Rites, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Su Ting, Duke of Xuwenxian and Minister of Rites, died.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙子，吐蕃大將悉諾邏恭祿及燭龍莽布支攻陷瓜州，執刺史田元獻及河西節度使王君𡙟之父，進攻玉門軍；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingzi, the Tibetan generals Xinuo-luo Gonglu and Zhulong Mangbuzhi captured Guazhou, seized Prefect Tian Yuanxian and the father of Hexi Military Commissioner Wang Jun, and advanced to attack Yumen Army;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingzi, Tibetan generals Xinuo-luo Gonglu and Zhulong Mangbuzhi took Guazhou, captured Prefect Tian Yuanxian and Wang Jun's father, and pressed on against Yumen Army;

sentences.zh: 縱所虜僧伽歸涼州，謂君𡙟曰：「將軍常以忠通許國，何不一戰！」

translations.literal: they released the captive monk Jia to Liangzhou and said to Jun: "The general has always pledged loyalty to the state—why not fight one battle!"
translations.idiomatic: They sent a captured monk to Liangzhou to tell Jun, "You always boast loyalty to the throne—why not fight?"

sentences.zh: 君𡙟登城西望而泣，竟不敢不兵。

translations.literal: Jun climbed the west wall, looked out, and wept; in the end he did not dare send troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jun climbed the west wall, looked out, and wept; in the end he did not dare march out to fight.

sentences.zh: 莽布支別攻常樂縣，縣令賈師順帥眾拒守。

translations.literal: Mangbuzhi separately attacked Changle County; Magistrate Jia Shishun led the people in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Mangbuzhi separately attacked Changle County; Magistrate Jia Shishun led the defense.

sentences.zh: 及瓜州陷，悉諾邏悉兵會攻之。

translations.literal: When Guazhou fell, Xinuo-luo gathered all his troops to join in the attack.
translations.idiomatic: After Guazhou fell, Xinuo-luo concentrated his forces against it.

sentences.zh: 旬餘日，吐蕃力盡，不能克，使人說降之；

translations.literal: After more than ten days the Tibetans' strength was exhausted and they could not take it; they sent men to persuade surrender;
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days the Tibetans were exhausted and could not take the city; they sent envoys to offer terms;

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: he would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Jia refused.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃曰：「明府既不降，宜斂城中財相贈，吾當退。」

translations.literal: The Tibetans said: "Since the magistrate will not surrender, he ought to gather the city's wealth as a gift; then we shall withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans said, "If you will not surrender, gather the city's wealth as a gift and we will withdraw."

sentences.zh: 師順請脫士卒衣；

translations.literal: Shishun asked that the soldiers' clothing be stripped off;
translations.idiomatic: Shishun asked only that the soldiers' clothes be taken;

sentences.zh: 悉諾邏知無財，乃引去，毀瓜州城。

translations.literal: Xinuo-luo knew there was no wealth and then led his men away, destroying Guazhou's walls.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing there was no wealth, Xinuo-luo withdrew and destroyed the walls of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 師順遽開門，收器械，修守備；

translations.literal: Shishun hastily opened the gates, gathered weapons, and repaired defenses;
translations.idiomatic: Shishun at once opened the gates, gathered arms, and repaired the defenses;

sentences.zh: 虜果復遣精騎還，視城中，知有備，乃去。

translations.literal: the barbarians indeed sent elite cavalry back; seeing the city prepared, they left.
translations.idiomatic: the Tibetans did send elite cavalry back, but seeing the city ready, they left.

sentences.zh: 師順，岐州人也。

translations.literal: Shishun was a man of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shishun was from Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥默啜之強也，迫奪鐵勒之地，故回紇、契苾、思結、渾四部度磧徙居甘、涼之間以避之。

translations.literal: Earlier when the Turk Mo-ch'o was strong, he seized Tiele lands by force; therefore the four tribes—the Uighurs, Qibi, Sijie, and Hun—crossed the desert and moved to live between Gan and Liang to escape him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turk qaghan Mo-ch'o was at his height he seized Tiele lands, so the Uighurs, Qibi, Sijie, and Hun crossed the desert and settled between Gan and Liang to escape him.

sentences.zh: 王君𡙟微時，往來四部，為其所輕；

translations.literal: When Wang Jun was young he traveled among the four tribes and was looked down on by them;
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Wang Jun had dealings with the four tribes and was despised by them;

sentences.zh: 及為河西節度使，以法繩之。

translations.literal: when he became Hexi Military Commissioner he restrained them with the law.
translations.idiomatic: when he became Hexi commissioner he held them strictly to the law.

sentences.zh: 四部恥怨，密遣使詣東都自訴。

translations.literal: The four tribes, shamed and resentful, secretly sent envoys to the eastern capital to plead their case.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated and angry, the four tribes secretly sent envoys to the eastern capital to complain.

sentences.zh: 君𡙟遽發驛奏「四部難制，潛有叛計。」

translations.literal: Jun hastily sent a relay memorial: "The four tribes are hard to control and secretly harbor plans of rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Jun at once sent an urgent memorial: "The four tribes are ungovernable and secretly plot rebellion."

sentences.zh: 上遣中使往察之，諸部竟不得直。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to investigate; the tribes in the end could not obtain justice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy to investigate, but the tribes never got a fair hearing.

sentences.zh: 於是瀚海大都督回紇承宗流瀼州，渾大德流吉州，賀蘭都督契苾承明流籐州，盧山都督思結歸國流瓊州；

translations.literal: thereupon Chengzong of the Uighurs, Grand Protector-General of Hanhai, was banished to Rangzhou; Dadé of the Hun to Jizhou; Chengming of the Qibi, Protector-General of Helan, to Tengzhou; and Guiguo of the Sijie, Protector-General of Lushan, to Qiongzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong of the Uighurs was banished to Rangzhou, Dadé of the Hun to Jizhou, Chengming of the Qibi to Tengzhou, and Guiguo of the Sijie to Qiongzhou;

sentences.zh: 以回紇伏帝難為瀚海大都督。

translations.literal: Fudinan of the Uighurs was made Grand Protector-General of Hanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Fudinan of the Uighurs was appointed Grand Protector-General of Hanhai.

sentences.zh: 己卯，貶右散騎常侍李令問為撫州別駕，坐其子與承宗交遊故也。

translations.literal: On jimao Li Lingwen, Right Regular Attendant, was demoted to Vice-Prefect of Fuzhou because his son had associated with Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Li Lingwen, Right Regular Attendant, was demoted to vice-prefect of Fuzhou because his son had befriended Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，突厥毘伽可汗遣其大臣梅祿啜入貢。

translations.literal: On bingxu the Turk Qaghan Bilge sent his minister Meiluochuo to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the Turk Qaghan Bilge sent his minister Meiluochuo with tribute.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃之寇瓜州也，遺毘伽書，欲與之俱入寇，毘伽並獻其書。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans raided Guazhou they sent Bilge a letter wishing to invade together; Bilge presented the letter as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet attacked Guazhou it had written Bilge proposing a joint invasion; Bilge handed over the letter with his tribute.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，聽於西受降城為互市，每歲繼縑帛數十萬匹就市戎馬，以助軍旅，且為監牧之種，由是國馬益壯焉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and permitted a market at West Surrender City; each year several hundred thousand bolts of silk were sent to buy barbarian horses, to aid the armies and also to provide breeding stock for the imperial pastures—whereby state horses grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him and allowed trade at West Surrender City; each year hundreds of thousands of bolts of silk were sent to buy horses for the armies and imperial studs, and from this the state's horses grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 閏月，庚子，吐蕃贊普與突騎施蘇祿圍安西城，安西副大都護趙頤貞擊破之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on gengzi, the Tibetan tsenpo and the Turgesh Suolu besieged Anxi City; Zhao Yizhen, Vice Protector-General of Anxi, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on gengzi, the Tibetan emperor and Turgesh Suolu besieged Anxi; Vice Protector-General Zhao Yizhen routed them.

sentences.zh: 回紇承宗族子瀚海司馬護輸，糾合黨眾為承宗報仇。

translations.literal: Hushu, a clansman of the Uighur Chengzong and Hanhai Army Major, gathered partisans to avenge Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: Hushu, a kinsman of Chengzong and major in the Hanhai command, rallied supporters to avenge him.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃遣使間道詣突厥，王君𡙟帥精騎邀之於肅州。

translations.literal: It happened that Tibet sent envoys by a secret route to the Turks; Wang Jun led elite cavalry to intercept them at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet had sent envoys by a secret route to the Turks; Wang Jun led elite cavalry to intercept them at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 還，至甘州南鞏筆驛，護輸伏兵突起，奪君𡙟旌節，先殺其判官宋貞，剖其心曰：「始謀者汝也。」

translations.literal: On the return, at Gongbi Post south of Ganzhou, Hushu's ambush sprang up, seized Jun's credentials of office, and first killed his aide Song Zhen, cutting open his heart and saying: "You were the first to plot this."
translations.idiomatic: On the way back, at Gongbi Post south of Ganzhou, Hushu's ambush struck, seized Jun's credentials, and first killed his aide Song Zhen, cutting out his heart and crying, "You were the one who plotted this!"

sentences.zh: 君𡙟帥左右數十人力戰，自朝至晡，左右盡死。

translations.literal: Jun led several dozen attendants in fierce fighting from morning until afternoon; his attendants all died.
translations.idiomatic: Jun fought on with a few dozen men from morning until afternoon until all his companions were dead.

sentences.zh: 護輸殺君𡙟，載其屍奔吐蕃；

translations.literal: Hushu killed Jun, loaded his corpse, and fled toward Tibet;
translations.idiomatic: Hushu killed Jun, took his body, and fled toward Tibet;

sentences.zh: 涼州兵追及之，護輸棄屍而走。

translations.literal: Liangzhou troops overtook him; Hushu abandoned the corpse and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou troops caught up; Hushu abandoned the body and escaped.

sentences.zh: 庚申，車駕發東都，冬，己卯，至西京。

translations.literal: On gengshen the imperial carriage set out from the eastern capital; in winter, on jimao, it reached the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the court left the eastern capital; in winter, on jimao, it reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以左金吾衛大將軍信安王禕為朔方節度等副大使。

translations.literal: On xinsi the Prince of Xin'an, Li Yi, Left General of the Golden Guard, was made deputy commissioner of Shuofang and related commands.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Prince Xin'an Li Yi, Left General of the Golden Guard, was made deputy commissioner for Shuofang and related commands.

sentences.zh: 禕，恪之孫也。

translations.literal: Yi was a grandson of Li Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was a grandson of Li Ke.

sentences.zh: 以朔方節度使蕭嵩為河西節度等副大使。

translations.literal: Shuofang Military Commissioner Xiao Song was made deputy commissioner of Hexi and related commands.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang commissioner Xiao Song was made deputy commissioner for Hexi and related commands.

sentences.zh: 時王君𡙟新敗，河、隴震駭。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Jun had just been defeated; He and Long circuits were shaken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun had just been killed and the He and Long frontier was in shock.

sentences.zh: 嵩引刑部員外郎裴寬為判官，與君𡙟判官牛仙客俱掌軍政，人心浸安。

translations.literal: Song brought in Pei Kuan of the Ministry of Justice as aide, and together with Jun's former aide Niu Xianke they managed military affairs; hearts gradually grew calm.
translations.idiomatic: Song took Pei Kuan of the Ministry of Justice as his aide; together with Jun's former aide Niu Xianke they ran military affairs, and morale slowly steadied.

sentences.zh: 寬，漼之從弟也。

translations.literal: Kuan was a younger cousin of Li Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was a younger cousin of Li Chui.

sentences.zh: 仙客本鶉觚小吏，以才幹軍功累遷至河西節度判官，為君𡙟腹心。

translations.literal: Xianke had originally been a petty clerk of Gaogu; through ability and military merit he rose step by step to Hexi Military Commission aide and was Jun's trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke had begun as a minor clerk in Gaogu and rose through talent and battlefield merit to Hexi aide; he had been Jun's closest confidant.

sentences.zh: 嵩又奏以建康軍使河北張守珪為瓜州刺史，帥餘眾築故城。

translations.literal: Song also memorialized appointing Zhang Shougui of Hebei, commissioner of Jiankang Army, as Prefect of Guazhou, to lead the remaining troops in rebuilding the old city.
translations.idiomatic: Song also recommended Zhang Shougui of Hebei, commander of Jiankang Army, as prefect of Guazhou to rebuild the old city with the survivors.

sentences.zh: 板干裁立，吐蕃猝至，城中相顧失色，莫有鬥志。

translations.literal: Planking and beams had barely been set up when Tibetans arrived suddenly; within the city men looked at one another in dismay and none had fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The timbers had barely been raised when Tibetans appeared; the garrison looked at one another in dismay and none would fight.

sentences.zh: 守珪曰：「彼眾我寡，人瘡痍之餘，不可以矢刃相持，當以奇計取勝。」

translations.literal: Shougui said: "They are many and we few; the people are still wounded and weary—we cannot contend with blades and arrows but must win by a stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Shougui said, "They outnumber us and our men are exhausted—we cannot fight them head-on; we must win by stratagem."

sentences.zh: 乃於城上置酒作樂。

translations.literal: He then set out wine on the wall and made music.
translations.idiomatic: He had wine set out on the walls and music played.

sentences.zh: 虜疑其有備，不敢攻而退。

translations.literal: The barbarians suspected he was prepared, did not dare attack, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans suspected a trap, dared not attack, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 守珪縱兵擊之，虜敗走。

translations.literal: Shougui loosed his troops to strike them; the barbarians were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui then sallied forth and routed them.

sentences.zh: 守珪乃修復城市，收合流散，皆復舊業。

translations.literal: Shougui then restored the city, gathered the scattered, and all resumed their former livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the city, gathered the displaced, and restored their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其功，以瓜州為都督府，以守珪為都督。

translations.literal: The court praised his achievement, made Guazhou a Protectorate command, and appointed Shougui Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his feat, made Guazhou a protectorate, and appointed Shougui its protector-general.

sentences.zh: 悉諾邏威名甚盛，蕭嵩縱反間於吐蕃，雲與中國通謀，贊普召而誅之；

translations.literal: Xinuo-luo's fame was very great; Xiao Song spread counterintelligence in Tibet saying he was in secret collusion with China; the tsenpo summoned and executed him;
translations.idiomatic: Xinuo-luo's renown was great; Xiao Song spread word in Tibet that he was plotting with China; the tsenpo summoned and executed him;

sentences.zh: 吐蕃由是少衰。

translations.literal: Tibet from this somewhat declined.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan power waned somewhat from this.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊寅，制以吐蕃為邊患，令隴右道及諸軍團兵五萬六千人，河西道及諸軍團兵四萬人，又征關中兵萬人集臨洮，朔方兵二萬人集會州防秋，至冬初，無寇而罷；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuyin, an edict, because Tibet was a frontier menace, ordered fifty-six thousand militia of Longyou Circuit and its armies, forty thousand of Hexi Circuit and its armies, and also drafted ten thousand Guanzhong troops to assemble at Lintao and twenty thousand Shuofang troops to assemble at Huizhou for autumn defense; by early winter, if there was no raid, they were dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuyin, an edict ordered fifty-six thousand Longyou troops, forty thousand Hexi troops, ten thousand Guanzhong men to Lintao, and twenty thousand Shuofang men to Huizhou for autumn defense against Tibet; if no enemy appeared by early winter, they were sent home;

sentences.zh: 伺虜入寇，互出兵腹背擊之。

translations.literal: when barbarians invaded, forces from several directions were to strike them front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: when the enemy invaded, columns were to strike them from front and rear.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，上幸驪山溫泉；

translations.literal: On yihai the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 丙戌，還宮。

translations.literal: on bingxu he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on bingxu he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬寅，安西副大都護趙頤貞敗吐蕃於曲子城。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renyin, Zhao Yizhen, Vice Protector-General of Anxi, defeated the Tibetans at Quzi City.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renyin, Vice Protector-General of Anxi Zhao Yizhen defeated the Tibetans at Quzi City.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以魏州刺史宇文融為戶部侍郎兼魏州刺史，充河北道宣撫使。

translations.literal: On jiayin Yuwen Rong, Prefect of Weizhou, was made Vice Minister of Revenue while retaining Weizhou and appointed Pacification Commissioner of Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Yuwen Rong was made Vice Minister of Revenue while remaining prefect of Weizhou and was appointed pacification commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，春、瀧等州獠陳行范、廣州獠馮璘、何游魯反，陷四十餘城。

translations.literal: On yimao the Liao of Chun, Long, and other prefectures—Chen Xingfan, Feng Lin of Guangzhou, and He Youlu—rebelled and seized more than forty cities.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the Liao chiefs Chen Xingfan, Feng Lin, and He Youlu rebelled in the south and seized more than forty cities.

sentences.zh: 行范稱帝，游魯稱定國大將軍，璘稱南越王，欲據嶺表；

translations.literal: Xingfan declared himself emperor, Youlu styled himself Grand General Who Settles the State, and Lin styled himself King of Southern Yue, intending to hold the Lingnan region;
translations.idiomatic: Xingfan declared himself emperor, Youlu took the title Grand General Who Settles the State, and Lin called himself King of Southern Yue, aiming to hold the Lingnan region;

sentences.zh: 命內侍楊思勖發桂州及嶺北近道兵討之。

translations.literal: the palace attendant Yang Sixu was ordered to raise troops from Guizhou and nearby routes north of the ranges to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ordered the palace attendant Yang Sixu to raise troops from Guizhou and nearby districts to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以魏州刺史宇文融檢校汴州刺史，充河南北溝渠堤堰決九河使。

translations.literal: On bingyin Yuwen Rong, while Prefect of Weizhou, was made acting Prefect of Bianzhou and Commissioner for Dikes, Canals, and the Nine Rivers of North and South Henan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Yuwen Rong was made acting prefect of Bianzhou and commissioner for Henan's rivers, canals, and dikes.

sentences.zh: 融請用《禹貢》九河故道開稻田，並回易陸運錢，官收其利；

translations.literal: Rong asked to open rice fields along the old courses of the Nine Rivers in the Yugong, and also to convert land-transport funds, the government taking the profit;
translations.idiomatic: Rong proposed reopening the Nine Rivers of the Yugong for rice fields and diverting land-transport funds for the state to profit;

sentences.zh: 興役不息，事多不就。

translations.literal: labor projects never ceased, yet most undertakings were not accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: corvée never stopped, yet little was achieved.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬申，以尚書右丞相致仕張說兼集賢院學士。

translations.literal: In the second month, on renshen, Zhang Shuo, retired Right Chief Minister of the Secretariat, was also made Academician of the Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renshen, retired Right Chief Minister Zhang Shuo was also made an academician of the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 說雖罷政事，專文史之任，朝廷每有大事，上常遣中使訪之。

translations.literal: Although Shuo had left political affairs, he devoted himself to literary and historical duties; whenever the court had a great matter, the emperor often sent palace envoys to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Though out of politics, he devoted himself to letters; on great occasions the emperor often sent envoys to ask his counsel.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，改擴騎為左右羽林軍飛騎。

translations.literal: On renchen the Kuozhan Cavalry were renamed Flying Cavalry of the Left and Right Feathered Forest Armies.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the expanded cavalry were reorganized as the Flying Cavalry of the Left and Right Feathered Forest Armies.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，吐蕃大將悉末郎寇瓜州，都督張守珪擊走之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Tibetan general Ximolang raided Guazhou; Protector-General Zhang Shougui drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the Tibetan general Ximolang raided Guazhou; Protector-General Zhang Shougui repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，河西節度使蕭嵩、隴右節度使張忠亮大破吐蕃於渴波谷；

translations.literal: On yisi Hexi Military Commissioner Xiao Song and Longyou Military Commissioner Zhang Zhongliang inflicted a great defeat on the Tibetans at Kebo Valley;
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Xiao Song of Hexi and Zhang Zhongliang of Longyou routed the Tibetans at Kebo Valley;

sentences.zh: 忠亮追之，拔其大莫門城，擒獲甚眾，焚其駱駝橋而還。

translations.literal: Zhongliang pursued them, took their city of Damen, captured many, burned their Camel Bridge, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang pursued, took Damen, captured many prisoners, burned the Camel Bridge, and returned.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙巳，特進張說上《開元大衍歷》，行之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yisi, Zhang Shuo, Special Advance, presented the Kaiyuan Dayan Calendar; it was put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yisi Zhang Shuo presented the Kaiyuan Dayan Calendar, and it was adopted.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，右金吾將軍杜賓客破吐蕃於祁連城下。

translations.literal: On xinmao Du Binke, Right General of the Golden Guard, defeated the Tibetans below Qilian City.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Du Binke, Right General of the Golden Guard, defeated the Tibetans below Qilian City.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃復入寇，蕭嵩遣賓客將強弩四千擊之。

translations.literal: At this time Tibet again invaded; Xiao Song sent Binke with four thousand strong crossbowmen to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet had invaded again; Xiao Song sent Binke with four thousand crossbowmen against them.

sentences.zh: 戰自辰至暮，吐蕃大潰，獲其大將一人；

translations.literal: Battle lasted from chen hour to evening; the Tibetans were utterly routed and one of their generals was captured;
translations.idiomatic: Fighting lasted from morning to evening; the Tibetans broke and one general was captured;

sentences.zh: 虜散走投山，哭聲四合。

translations.literal: the barbarians scattered and fled into the mountains; cries of grief sounded on every side.
translations.idiomatic: the enemy fled into the hills in all directions, wailing on every side.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己卯，上幸驪山溫泉；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jimao, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jimao, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 己丑，還宮。

translations.literal: on jichou he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on jichou he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸巳，以河西節度副大使蕭嵩為兵部尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on guisi, Xiao Song, deputy commissioner of Hexi, was made Minister of War and Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on guisi Hexi deputy commissioner Xiao Song was made Minister of War and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙寅，敕：「長徵兵無有還期，人情難堪；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingyin, an edict stated: "Long-campaign soldiers have no date of return; human feelings can hardly bear it;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingyin an edict declared, "Soldiers on long campaigns have no set date of return, and morale cannot endure it;

sentences.zh: 宜分五番，歲遣一番還家洗沐，五年酬勳五轉。」

translations.literal: They should be divided into five rotations; each year one rotation should be sent home to bathe and rest; in five years reward merit with five promotions."
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers should serve in five rotations, with one rotation sent home each year to rest; after five years they would receive five merit promotions."

sentences.zh: 是歲，制戶籍三歲一定，分為九等。

translations.literal: That year, it was decreed that household registers be fixed every three years and divided into nine grades.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict required household registers to be reassessed every three years and ranked in nine grades.

sentences.zh: 楊思勖討陳行范，至瀧州，破之，擒何游魯、馮璘。

translations.literal: Yang Sixiu campaigned against Chen Xingfan, reached Long Prefecture, defeated him, and captured He Youlu and Feng Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sixiu attacked Chen Xingfan, reached Long Prefecture, routed his forces, and captured He Youlu and Feng Lin.

sentences.zh: 行范逃於雲際、盤遼二洞，思勖追捕，竟生擒，斬之，凡斬首六萬。

translations.literal: Xingfan fled to the two caves of Yunji and Panliao; Sixiu pursued and in the end captured him alive and beheaded him; in all six myriad heads were severed.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfan fled to the Yunji and Panliao caves; Sixiu hunted him down, took him alive, executed him, and severed sixty thousand heads in all.

sentences.zh: 思勖為人嚴，偏裨白事者不敢仰視，故用兵所向有功。

translations.literal: Sixiu as a man was stern; staff officers reporting business dared not look up at him, and therefore in employing troops wherever he went he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Sixiu was a severe man; subordinate officers reporting to him dared not meet his gaze, and so his campaigns were consistently successful.

sentences.zh: 然性忍酷，所得俘虜，或生剝面皮，或以刀剺髮際，掣去頭皮；

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was cruel and harsh; captives he took were sometimes flayed alive of facial skin, or with a knife scored the hairline and tore off the scalp;
translations.idiomatic: But he was cruel by nature: captives were sometimes flayed alive, or a knife was run along the hairline to peel off the scalp;

sentences.zh: 蠻夷憚之。

translations.literal: The barbarians feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The southern tribes feared him.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，丁卯，巂州都督張守素破西南蠻，拔昆明及鹽城，殺獲萬人。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on dingmao, Protectorate-General of Xi Prefecture Zhang Shousu defeated the southwestern barbarians, took Kunming and Yancheng, and killed and captured ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on dingmao, Zhang Shousu, military governor of Xi Prefecture, defeated the southwestern tribes, captured Kunming and Salt City, and killed or captured ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 三月，瓜州都督張守珪、沙州刺史賈師順擊吐蕃大同軍，大破之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Protectorate-General of Gua Prefecture Zhang Shougui and Prefect of Sha Prefecture Jia Shishun attacked the Tibetan Datong Army and greatly defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zhang Shougui, governor of Gua Prefecture, and Jia Shishun, prefect of Sha Prefecture, attacked the Tibetan Datong Army and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，朔方節度使信安王禕攻吐蕃石堡城，拔之。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Military Commissioner of Shuofang the Prince of Xin'an Yi attacked the Tibetan Stone Fortress City and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the Prince of Xin'an Yi, military commissioner of Shuofang, attacked the Tibetan stronghold of Stone Fortress City and captured it.

sentences.zh: 初，吐蕃陷石堡城，留兵據之，侵擾河右。

translations.literal: Earlier the Tibetans had captured Stone Fortress City, left troops to hold it, and harassed the lands west of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Tibetans had seized Stone Fortress City, garrisoned it, and raided the Hexi region.

sentences.zh: 上命禕與河西、隴右同議攻取。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yi to consult with Hexi and Longyou jointly on attacking and taking it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yi to consult with the Hexi and Longyou commands on a joint assault.

sentences.zh: 諸將鹹以為石堡據險而道遠，攻之不克，將無以自還，且宜按兵觀釁。

translations.literal: The generals all thought that Stone Fortress occupied perilous ground and the route was far; if the attack did not succeed, the generals would have no way to return, and they should rather halt the army and watch for an opening.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all argued that Stone Fortress was strong and distant, that failure would leave them no retreat, and that they should hold their forces and wait for an opportunity.

sentences.zh: 禕不聽，引兵深入，急攻拔之，仍分兵據守要害，令虜不得前。

translations.literal: Yi would not listen, led troops deep in, pressed the attack and took it, then divided troops to hold key points and made the enemy unable to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yi refused to listen, marched deep into enemy territory, stormed and captured the fortress, then deployed garrisons at key positions to block the Tibetans' advance.

sentences.zh: 自是河隴諸軍游弈，拓境千餘里。

translations.literal: From this the armies of Hexi and Longyou ranged in patrol and extended the frontier more than a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Hexi and Longyou forces patrolled the frontier and expanded the border by more than a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 上聞，大悅，更命石堡城曰振武軍。

translations.literal: The emperor heard this and was greatly pleased, and renamed Stone Fortress City Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly pleased at the news, the emperor renamed Stone Fortress City the Zhenwu Army garrison.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，國子祭酒楊瑒言，以為：「省司奏限天下明經、進士及第，每年不過百人。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education Yang Yan remarked, considering: "The provincial offices memorialized limiting Mingjing and Jinshi degree-holders throughout the realm to no more than a hundred per year.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Yang Yan, chancellor of the Directorate of Education, argued: "Provincial offices have proposed capping Mingjing and Jinshi graduates empire-wide at no more than one hundred per year.

sentences.zh: 竊見流外出身，每歲二千餘人，而明經、進士不能居其什一，則是服勤道業之士不如胥史之得仕也。

translations.literal: I have observed that those entering office from exile each year number more than two thousand, while Mingjing and Jinshi cannot occupy one tenth of that — then those who diligently serve the Way are inferior to clerks in gaining office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet more than two thousand entrants from administrative exile appointment each year far exceed Mingjing and Jinshi combined — meaning scholars devoted to learning fare worse than petty clerks in winning office.

sentences.zh: 臣恐儒風浸墜，廉恥日衰。

translations.literal: Your subject fears Confucian influence will gradually sink and integrity and shame daily decline.
translations.idiomatic: I fear Confucian standards will erode and public morals will decay.

sentences.zh: 若以出身人太多，則應諸色裁損，不應獨抑明經、進士也。」

translations.literal: If there are too many entrants, then all categories should be cut back, and one should not suppress Mingjing and Jinshi alone."
translations.idiomatic: If there are too many appointees, quotas should be cut across all routes — not only for Mingjing and Jinshi."

sentences.zh: 又奏「主司貼試明經，不務求述作本指，專取難知，問以孤經絕句或年月日；

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The chief examiners in the attached Mingjing test do not seek the basic intent of exposition and composition, but exclusively take what is hard to know, asking isolated sentences, obscure passages, or dates;
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "Mingjing examiners ignored the purpose of classical exposition and instead tested obscure trivia — isolated sentences, recondite passages, or calendar dates;

sentences.zh: 請自今並貼平文。」

translations.literal: He requested that from now on only straightforward passages be attached."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that hereafter only ordinary passages be used in the attached test."

sentences.zh: 上甚然之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚午，禘於太廟。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on gengwu, the di sacrifice was performed at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengwu, the di rite was held at the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 唐初，祫則序昭穆，禘則各祀於其室。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang, for the xia rite the zhao and mu were ordered, but for the di rite each was sacrificed to in its own chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tang, the xia rite ranked ancestors by zhao and mu sequence, while the di rite sacrificed to each in its own shrine chamber.

sentences.zh: 至是，太常少卿韋縚等奏：「如此，禘與常饗不異；

translations.literal: At this time Vice Minister of Rites Wei Tao and others memorialized: "In this way the di rite would not differ from ordinary offerings;
translations.idiomatic: At this point Vice Minister of Rites Wei Tao and others argued: "Under this practice the di rite would be no different from regular offerings;

sentences.zh: 請禘祫皆序昭穆。」

translations.literal: we request that both di and xia rites order the zhao and mu."
translations.idiomatic: we ask that both di and xia rites follow zhao-mu ordering."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 綏，安石之兄子也。

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: Sui was the elder brother's son of Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: Sui was the nephew of Wei Anshi.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬辰，復置十道及京、都兩畿按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renchen, the ten circuits and the two capitals' metropolitan regions' inspection commissioners were reestablished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renchen, inspection commissioners for the ten circuits and the two metropolitan regions around the capitals were restored.

sentences.zh: 初，張說、張嘉貞、李元紘、杜暹相繼為相用事，源乾曜以清謹自守，常讓事於說等，唯諾署名而已。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Yue, Zhang Jiazhen, Li Yuanhong, and Du Xian succeeded one another as chancellors in power; Yuan Qianyao guarded himself with purity and prudence, often yielding affairs to Yue and the others, merely assenting and signing his name.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Zhang Yue, Zhang Jiazhen, Li Yuanhong, and Du Xian had held real power in succession; Yuan Qianyao, cautious and discreet, usually deferred to them and merely signed his name in assent.

sentences.zh: 元紘、暹議事多異同，遂有隙，更相奏列。

translations.literal: Yuanhong and Xian often differed in deliberating affairs; eventually there was a rift, and they repeatedly impeached each other.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong and Xian frequently clashed in policy debates, grew estranged, and repeatedly denounced each other.

sentences.zh: 上不悅，六月，甲戌，貶黃門侍郎、同平章事杜暹荊州長史，中書侍郎、同平章事李元紘曹州刺史，罷乾曜兼侍中，止為左丞相；

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; in the sixth month, on jiaxu, Yellow Gate Vice Minister and Fellow Grand Councillor Du Xian was demoted to chief administrator of Jing Prefecture, Secretariat Vice Minister and Fellow Grand Councillor Li Yuanhong to prefect of Cao Prefecture, Qianyao was removed from his concurrent post as Palace Secretary and remained only as Left Chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, the emperor in the sixth month, on jiaxu, demoted Du Xian from vice minister and grand councillor to chief administrator of Jing Prefecture, and Li Yuanhong to prefect of Cao Prefecture; Qianyao lost his concurrent post as Palace Secretary and remained only as Left Chancellor;

sentences.zh: 以戶部侍郎宇文融為黃門侍郎，兵部侍部裴光庭為中書侍郎，並同平章事；

translations.literal: Households Vice Minister Yuwen Rong was made Yellow Gate Vice Minister, and Ministry of War Vice Minister Pei Guangting was made Secretariat Vice Minister — both as Fellow Grand Councillors;
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Rong was promoted from vice minister of revenue to vice minister of the Yellow Gate, and Pei Guangting from vice minister of war to vice minister of the Secretariat — both as grand councillors;

sentences.zh: 蕭嵩兼中書令，遙領河西。

translations.literal: Xiao Song was additionally made Secretariat Director and held Hexi in title from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Song was also made director of the Secretariat with nominal command over Hexi.

sentences.zh: 開府王毛仲與龍武將軍葛福順為婚。

translations.literal: Wang Maozhong, holder of the Kaifu title, became related by marriage to Longwu General Ge Fushun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maozhong, a kaifu noble, arranged a marriage alliance with Longwu General Ge Fushun.

sentences.zh: 毛仲為上所信任，言無不從，故北門諸將多附之，進退唯其指使。

translations.literal: Maozhong was trusted by the emperor and nothing he said was refused; therefore the generals of the Northern Gate largely attached to him, and promotion and demotion followed his direction alone.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong enjoyed the emperor's full trust and always got his way, so Northern Gate generals clustered around him and careers rose or fell at his command.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎齊澣乘間言於上曰：「福順典禁兵，不宜與毛仲為婚。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Qi Huan, seizing an opportunity, said to the emperor: "Fushun commands the forbidden troops and should not marry into Maozhong's family.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing an opportunity, Vice Minister of Personnel Qi Huan told the emperor, "Fushun commands the palace guard and should not marry into Maozhong's family.

sentences.zh: 毛仲小人，寵過則生奸；

translations.literal: Maozhong is a petty man; excessive favor will breed treachery;
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong is a base favorite; too much favor breeds intrigue;

sentences.zh: 不早為之，恐成後患。」

translations.literal: if this is not dealt with early, I fear it will become a later disaster."
translations.idiomatic: if you do not act soon, I fear future trouble."

sentences.zh: 上悅曰：「知卿忠誠，朕徐思其宜。」

translations.literal: The emperor, pleased, said: "I know your loyalty; I shall slowly consider what is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, pleased, replied, "I know you are loyal; I will consider the proper course in time."

sentences.zh: 澣曰：「君不密則失臣，願陛下密之。」

translations.literal: Huan said: "If the ruler is not secret he loses his minister; I wish Your Majesty would keep this secret."
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "If the ruler is not discreet he loses loyal ministers; I beg Your Majesty to keep this confidential."

sentences.zh: 會大理丞麻察坐事左遷興州別駕，澣素與察善，出城餞之，因道禁中諫語；

translations.literal: It happened that Censorate Assistant Director Ma Cha, having erred in office, was demoted to vice-prefect of Xing Prefecture; Huan had long been friendly with Cha, went outside the city to see him off, and along the way spoke of his admonitions within the palace;
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ma Cha of the censorate was demoted to vice-prefect of Xing Prefecture for an offense; Huan, an old friend, saw him off outside the city and let slip his private advice to the emperor;

sentences.zh: 察性輕險，遽奏之。

translations.literal: Cha by nature was frivolous and rash, and immediately memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Cha, frivolous and untrustworthy by nature, immediately reported it.

sentences.zh: 上怒，召澣責之曰：「卿疑朕不密，而以語麻察，詎為密邪？

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, summoned Huan, and reproached him, saying: "You doubt that I am not secret, yet you spoke to Ma Cha — is that being secret?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily summoned Huan and rebuked him: "You feared I could not keep a secret, yet you told Ma Cha — was that discreet?

sentences.zh: 且察素無行，卿豈不知邪？」

translations.literal: Moreover Cha has long had no good conduct — do you not know that?"
translations.idiomatic: And Ma Cha's character has always been poor — did you not know that?"

sentences.zh: 澣頓首謝。

translations.literal: Huan kowtowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Huan kowtowed and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁巳，下制：「澣、察交構將相，離間君臣，澣可高州良德丞，察可潯州皇化尉。」

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingsi, an edict was issued: "Huan and Cha together plotted against chancellor and general and drove a wedge between ruler and minister; Huan is appointed Assistant of Liangde in Gao Prefecture, Cha is appointed District Captain of Huanghua in Xun Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingsi, an edict declared, "Huan and Cha had conspired against chancellors and generals and sowed discord between ruler and minister; Huan was demoted to assistant of Liangde in Gao Prefecture and Cha to district captain of Huanghua in Xun Prefecture."

sentences.zh: 八月，癸亥，上以生日宴百官於花萼樓下。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on guihai, on his birthday the emperor feasted the hundred officials below the Hua'e Tower.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guihai, the emperor hosted a birthday banquet for the officials below the Tower of Flowery Calyx.

sentences.zh: 左丞相乾曜、右丞相說帥百官上表，請以每歲八月五日為千秋節，佈於天下，咸令宴樂。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Qianyao and Right Chancellor Yue led the hundred officials in memorializing, requesting that the fifth day of the eighth month each year be made the Thousand-Autumn Festival, proclaimed throughout the realm, with all ordered to feast and rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Qianyao and Right Chancellor Yue led the officials in requesting that the fifth day of the eighth month be established as the Thousand-Autumn Festival, proclaimed empire-wide and marked with feasting and celebration.

sentences.zh: 尋又移社就千秋節。

translations.literal: Shortly after the She sacrifice was also moved to coincide with the Thousand-Autumn Festival.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the She sacrifice was shifted to the Thousand-Autumn Festival as well.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，工部尚書張嘉貞薨。
