translations.literal: On gengchen, Minister of Works Zhang Jiazhen passed away.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Minister of Works Zhang Jiazhen died.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞不營家產，有勸其市田宅者，嘉貞曰：「吾貴為將相，何憂寒餒！

translations.literal: Jiazhen did not accumulate family property; when someone urged him to buy fields and houses, Jiazhen said: "I am honored as chancellor and general — why worry about cold and hunger!
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen did not amass private wealth; when urged to buy land and property, he said, "As a chancellor and general, why should I fear want!

sentences.zh: 若其獲罪，雖有田宅，亦無所用。

translations.literal: If I should incur guilt, even were there fields and houses, they would be of no use.
translations.idiomatic: If I were condemned for crime, property would do me no good anyway.

sentences.zh: 比見朝士廣占良田，身沒之日，適足為無賴子弟酒色之資，吾不取之。」

translations.literal: Of late I have seen court gentlemen widely occupy good fields; on the day they die, those suffice only as resources for worthless sons and nephews for wine and women — I do not take that path."
translations.idiomatic: I have seen too many officials hoard fine estates that, after their death, only feed dissolute heirs in wine and pleasure — I want no part of that."

sentences.zh: 聞者是之。

translations.literal: Those who heard approved.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard praised him.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，敕以人間多盜鑄錢，始禁私賣銅鉛錫及以銅為器皿；

translations.literal: On xinsi, an edict stated that because among the people there was much illicit coin casting, private sale of copper, lead, and tin and the making of vessels from copper were first forbidden;
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi an edict noted widespread illegal coin casting and banned private sale of copper, lead, and tin and the manufacture of copper vessels;

sentences.zh: 其採銅鉛錫者，官為市取。

translations.literal: those who mined copper, lead, and tin — the government would purchase from them.
translations.idiomatic: miners of copper, lead, and tin would sell their output to the government.

sentences.zh: 宇文融性精敏，應對辯給，以治財賦得幸於上，始文置諸使，競為聚斂，由是百官浸失其職而上心益侈，百姓皆怨苦之。

translations.literal: Yuwen Rong by nature was keen and sharp, quick and eloquent in reply; by managing finances and taxes he gained favor with the emperor; at first he established various commissioners who vied in collecting revenue; from this the hundred officials gradually lost their duties while the emperor's heart grew more extravagant, and the common people all resented and suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Rong was sharp, quick-witted, and eloquent; by handling finance he won the emperor's favor. He established revenue commissioners who competed to squeeze the country, officials gradually lost their proper roles, the emperor grew more extravagant, and the people groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 為人疏躁多言，好自矜伐，在相位，謂人曰：「使吾居此數月，則海內無事矣。」

translations.literal: As a man he was careless, rash, and talkative, fond of praising himself; in the chancellor's post he said to people: "If I hold this position a few months, then within the seas there will be nothing untoward."
translations.idiomatic: He was reckless, volatile, and boastful; while chancellor he told people, "Give me a few months in this post and the empire will be at peace."

sentences.zh: 信安王禕，以軍功有寵於上，融疾之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xin'an Yi, through military merit had favor with the emperor; Rong resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xin'an Yi enjoyed imperial favor for his military achievements, and Yuwen Rong resented him.

sentences.zh: 禕入朝，融使御史李寅彈之，洩於所親。

translations.literal: When Yi entered court, Rong had Censor Li Yin impeach him, and this leaked to those close to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi came to court, Rong sent Censor Li Yin to impeach him, but the move leaked to Yi's friends.

sentences.zh: 禕聞之，先以白上。

translations.literal: Yi heard of it and first reported it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of it, Yi reported the matter to the emperor first.

sentences.zh: 明日，寅奏果入，上怒，九月，壬子，融坐貶汝州刺史，凡為相百日而罷。

translations.literal: The next day Yin's memorial indeed arrived; the emperor was angry; in the ninth month, on renzi, Rong on that account was demoted to prefect of Ru Prefecture; in all he had been chancellor a hundred days and was removed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Li Yin's memorial arrived as expected; the emperor was furious; in the ninth month, on renzi, Rong was demoted to prefect of Ru Prefecture — he had served as chancellor barely a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 是後言財利以取貴仕者，皆祖於融。

translations.literal: After this those who spoke of finances and profit to gain honored office all traced their model to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter everyone who pursued wealth and power through fiscal office took Yuwen Rong as their model.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊午朔，日有食之，不盡如鉤。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day wuwu, there was an eclipse of the sun, not fully like a hook.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day wuwu, there was a partial solar eclipse shaped like a hook.

sentences.zh: 宇文融既得罪，國用不足，上復思之，謂裴光庭等曰：「卿等皆言融之惡，朕既黜之矣，今國用不足，將若之何！

translations.literal: Yuwen Rong having already been punished, state revenue was insufficient; the emperor again thought of him and said to Pei Guangting and the others: "You all spoke of Rong's evils; I have already dismissed him; now state revenue is insufficient — what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Rong's disgrace, revenues ran short; the emperor thought of him again and said to Pei Guangting and the others, "You all denounced Rong's faults and I removed him — yet now the treasury is empty. What am I to do?

sentences.zh: 卿等何在佐朕？」

translations.literal: Where are you in assisting me?"
translations.idiomatic: What use are you in helping me govern?"

sentences.zh: 光庭等懼不能對。

translations.literal: Guangting and the others feared and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting and the others were afraid and had no answer.

sentences.zh: 會有飛狀告融贓賄事，又貶平樂尉。

translations.literal: It happened that an urgent report accused Rong of bribery and corruption; he was again demoted to district captain of Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an urgent denunciation charged Rong with bribery, and he was demoted again to district captain of Pingle.

sentences.zh: 至嶺外歲餘，司農少卿蔣岑奏融在汴州隱沒官錢巨萬計，制窮治其事，融坐流巖州，道卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year beyond the Ling passes, Vice Minister of Agriculture Jiang Cen memorialized that Rong in Bian Prefecture had concealed official funds amounting to tens of thousands; an edict thoroughly investigated the matter; Rong was sentenced to exile in Yan Prefecture and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later in the far south, Vice Minister of Agriculture Jiang Cen reported that Rong had embezzled tens of thousands of official funds in Bian Prefecture; ordered fully investigated, Rong was exiled to Yan Prefecture and died en route.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛卯，上行謁橋、定、獻、昭、乾五陵；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinmao, the emperor went to visit the five tombs: Qiao, Ding, Xian, Zhao, and Qian;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinmao, the emperor visited the five imperial tombs: Qiao, Ding, Xian, Zhao, and Qian;

sentences.zh: 戊申，還宮；

translations.literal: on wushen he returned to the palace;
translations.idiomatic: on wushen he went back to the palace;

sentences.zh: 赦天下，百姓今年地稅悉蠲其半。

translations.literal: he pardoned the realm, and the common people's land tax for that year was entirely remitted by half.
translations.idiomatic: he proclaimed a general amnesty and halved the year's land tax for all commoners.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛酉，上幸新豐溫泉；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on xinyou, the emperor visited the hot springs at Xinfeng;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinyou, the emperor went to the hot springs at Xinfeng;

sentences.zh: 壬申，還宮。

translations.literal: on renshen he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on renshen he went back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛卯，以裴光庭為侍中。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinmao, Pei Guangting was made Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinmao, Pei Guangting was appointed Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸酉，初令百官於春月旬休，選勝行樂，自宰相至員外郎，凡十二筵，各賜錢五千緡，上或御花萼樓邀其歸騎留飲，迭使起舞，盡歡而去。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guiyou, for the first time the hundred officials were ordered on spring monthly ten-day rests to choose scenic spots for pleasure; from chancellor down to outside-service gentlemen, twelve groups in all, each was granted five thousand strings of cash; the emperor sometimes mounted the Hua'e Tower to invite their returning mounts to stay and drink, sending them in turn to dance, and they departed fully satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guiyou, officials were first granted monthly spring holidays to enjoy scenic outings; from chancellors down to outside-service gentlemen, twelve parties in all received five thousand strings of cash each; the emperor sometimes watched from the Tower of Flowery Calyx and invited returning groups to stay for wine, calling for dances in turn until all departed in high spirits.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁酉，復給京官職田。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingyou, office fields for capital officials were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingyou, official land allotments for capital officials were restored.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁卯，築西京外郭，九旬而畢。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingmao, the outer wall of the Western Capital was built, and in ninety days it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingmao, construction of the outer wall of the Western Capital was completed in ninety days.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以裴光庭兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: On yichou, Pei Guangting was additionally made Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Pei Guangting was also made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 先是，選司注官，惟視其人之能否，或不次超遷，或老於下位，有出身二十餘年不得祿者；

translations.literal: Earlier, the selection office in appointing posts looked only at a man's ability or lack thereof; some were promoted out of turn, some aged in lower ranks — there were those who had entered office more than twenty years without receiving salary;
translations.idiomatic: Previously appointments depended only on perceived ability: some rose out of turn, others languished in low posts for decades without ever drawing salary;

sentences.zh: 又，州縣亦無等級，或自大入小，或初近後遠，皆無定制。

translations.literal: furthermore prefectures and districts also had no grades; some went from large to small, some from near at first to far later — all without fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: nor were prefecture and district posts ranked consistently — some moved from large to small jurisdictions, others from nearby to distant posts, with no fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 光庭始奏用循資格，各以罷官若干選而集，官高者選少，卑者選多，無問能否，選滿即注，限年躡級，毋得逾越，非負譴者，皆有升無降；

translations.literal: Guangting first memorialized using the precedence-by-qualification system: each gathered according to how many selections since leaving office; the higher the office the fewer selections, the lower the more; regardless of ability, when selections were full appointment followed; years limited step-by-step promotion, none might overstep; except those bearing censure, all had promotion without demotion;
translations.idiomatic: Guangting introduced the seniority system: officials would be ranked by accumulated waiting periods after leaving office — fewer cycles for higher ranks, more for lower ones — ability aside, appointment came when the wait was complete, promotion followed fixed year-in-grade rules with no skipping ahead, and except for the censured, advancement was automatic without demotion;

sentences.zh: 其庸愚沉滯者皆喜，謂之「聖書」，而才俊之士無不怨歎。

translations.literal: the mediocre, foolish, and stagnant all rejoiced and called it the "Sagely Document," while talented and outstanding gentlemen all without exception resented and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre officials stuck in low posts rejoiced and called it the "Sagely Edict," while able men lamented it everywhere.

sentences.zh: 宋璟爭之不能得。

translations.literal: Song Jing contested it but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing objected but could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 光庭又令流外行署亦過門下省審。

translations.literal: Guangting also ordered that external temporary appointments likewise pass through the Secretariat for review.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting also required temporary provincial appointees to be reviewed by the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五月，吐蕃遣使致書於境上求和。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Tibet sent envoys with a letter at the border seeking peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Tibet sent envoys to the frontier with a letter requesting peace.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹王李邵固遣可突干入貢，同平章事李元紘不禮焉。

translations.literal: Earlier the Khitan king Li Shaogu sent Ketuqian to present tribute; Fellow Grand Councillor Li Yuanhong did not treat him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Khitan king Li Shaogu had sent Ketuqian to pay tribute, but Grand Councillor Li Yuanhong slighted him.

sentences.zh: 左丞相張說謂人曰：「奚、契丹必叛。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Zhang Yue said to people: "The Xi and Khitan will surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Zhang Yue said, "The Xi and Khitan will revolt.

sentences.zh: 可突干狡而很，專其國政久矣，人心附之。

translations.literal: Ketuqian is crafty and obstinate; he has monopolized state affairs for long, and the people's hearts attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuqian is crafty and fierce; he has controlled the kingdom for years and enjoys popular support.

sentences.zh: 今失其心，必不來矣。」

translations.literal: Now having lost his heart, he will surely not come again."
translations.idiomatic: Having lost his goodwill, he will never return."

sentences.zh: 己酉，可突干弒邵固，帥其國人並脅奚眾叛降突厥，奚王李魯蘇及其妻韋氏、邵固妻陳氏皆來奔。

translations.literal: On jiyou Ketuqian assassinated Shaogu, led his countrymen and also coerced Xi multitudes to rebel and surrender to the Turks; Xi king Li Lusu and his wife Lady Wei, and Shaogu's wife Lady Chen, all came fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Ketuqian murdered Shaogu, rallied his people, forced the Xi to join him, and defected to the Turks; Xi king Li Lusu, his wife Lady Wei, and Shaogu's wife Lady Chen all fled to Tang.

sentences.zh: 制幽州長史趙含章討之，又命中書舍人裴寬、給事中薛侃等於關內、河東、河南、北分道募勇士。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chief Administrator of You Prefecture Zhao Hanzhang to campaign against them; the emperor also ordered Secretariat Drafter Pei Kuan, Supervising Secretary Xue Kan, and others in Guannei, Hedong, Henan, and the north to recruit brave men by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zhao Hanzhang, chief administrator of You Prefecture, to suppress them, and sent Secretariat Drafter Pei Kuan, Supervising Secretary Xue Kan, and others to recruit warriors separately in Guannei, Hedong, Henan, and the north.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙子，以單于大都護忠王浚領河北道行軍元帥，以御史大夫李朝隱、京兆尹裴胄先副之，帥十八總管以討奚、契丹。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingzi, Grand Protector-General of the Chanyu Protectorate Prince Zhong Jun was made chief commander of the Hebei field army; Censor-in-Chief Li Chaoyin and Prefect of Jingzhao Pei Zhou were first made his deputies; he led eighteen area commanders to campaign against the Xi and Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingzi, Prince Zhong Jun, grand protector of the Chanyu Protectorate, was named commander of the Hebei campaign army, with Censor-in-Chief Li Chaoyin and Jingzhao Prefect Pei Zhou as his deputies, leading eighteen area commanders against the Xi and Khitan.

sentences.zh: 命浚與百官相見於光順門。

translations.literal: Jun was ordered to meet the hundred officials at the Gate of Shun of Light.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun was presented to the officials at the Gate of Glorious Accord.

sentences.zh: 張說退，謂學士孫逖、韋述曰：「吾嘗觀太宗畫像，雅類忠王，此社稷之福也。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yue withdrew and said to Academicians Sun Di and Wei Shu: "I once viewed the portrait of Emperor Taizong — it greatly resembles Prince Zhong; this is the fortune of the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue withdrew and told Academicians Sun Di and Wei Shu, "I once saw Emperor Taizong's portrait — Prince Zhong looks much like him; that is a blessing for the realm."

sentences.zh: 可突干寇平盧，先鋒使張掖烏承玼破之於捺祿山。

translations.literal: Ke-tugan raided Pinglu; the vanguard commissioner Wu Chengchi of Zhangye defeated him at Naluo Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Ketugan raided Pinglu, but Wu Chengchi of Zhangye, the vanguard commissioner, routed him at Mount Naluo.

sentences.zh: 壬午，洛水溢，溺東都千餘家。

translations.literal: On renwu, the Luo River overflowed and drowned more than a thousand households in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, the Luo River burst its banks and submerged over a thousand homes in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，丁巳，以忠王浚兼河東道元帥，然竟不行。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on dingsi, Prince Zhong Jun was additionally made commander of the Hedong circuit, yet in the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, on dingsi, Prince Zhong Jun was also appointed commander of Hedong circuit—but he never actually went.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃兵數敗而懼，乃求和親。

translations.literal: The Tibetan army, repeatedly defeated, grew fearful and then sought marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: After several defeats, the Tibetans grew alarmed and sued for a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 忠王友皇甫惟明因奏事從容言和親之利。

translations.literal: Huangfu Weiming, companion to Prince Zhong, while reporting on business spoke at ease of the benefits of marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Weiming, Prince Zhong's companion, took occasion while presenting a memorial to speak calmly of the advantages of alliance through marriage.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「贊普嘗遺吾書悖慢，此何可捨！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The tsenpo once sent me a letter insolent and disrespectful—how can this be set aside!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Tibetan king once sent me an insulting letter—how can we simply overlook that!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「贊普當開元之初，年尚幼稚，安能為此書！

translations.literal: He replied: "At the opening of the Kaiyuan era the tsenpo was still young and immature—how could he have written such a letter!
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "At the beginning of Kaiyuan the Tibetan king was still a child—he could hardly have written such a letter!

sentences.zh: 殆邊將詐為之，欲以激怒陛下耳。

translations.literal: Likely frontier generals falsified it, wishing thereby to enrage Your Majesty, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier generals probably forged it, intending only to goad Your Majesty into anger.

sentences.zh: 夫邊境有事，則將吏得以因緣盜匿官物，妄述功狀以取勳爵。

translations.literal: When the border has affairs, then officers and clerks can by opportunity embezzle and conceal official goods, falsely narrate merit reports to obtain honors and noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier is in turmoil, officers and officials seize the chance to pilfer government stores and invent battle reports to win honors and titles.

sentences.zh: 此皆奸臣之利，非國家之福也。

translations.literal: These are all profits for treacherous ministers, not blessings for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Such gains accrue only to scheming officials—not to the nation's good.

sentences.zh: 兵連不解，日費千金，河西、隴右由茲困敝。

translations.literal: Arms joined without release, daily expense of a thousand in gold; Hexi and Longyou from this grew exhausted and impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: War dragged on without end, costing a thousand in gold each day, and Hexi and Longyou were worn down by it.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠命一使往視公主，因與贊普面相約結。

translations.literal: Your Majesty truly should command one envoy to go view the princess, and thereby with the tsenpo face to face make covenant and alliance.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would send an envoy to visit the princess and there face the Tibetan king to renew pledges—

sentences.zh: 使之稽顙稱臣，永息邊患，豈非御夷狄之長策乎！」

translations.literal: Cause him to knock his forehead and declare himself subject, forever still the border calamities—is this not the long strategy for controlling the barbarians of Yi and Di!"
translations.idiomatic: —and bow before you as a vassal, ending the border threat forever, would that not be the wisest way to manage the northern tribes!"

sentences.zh: 上悅，命惟明與內侍張元方使於吐蕃。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and commanded Weiming together with the inner attendant Zhang Yuanfang to serve as envoys to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and sent Weiming with the eunuch Zhang Yuanfang as envoys to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 贊普大喜，悉出貞觀以來所得敕書以示惟明。

translations.literal: The tsenpo greatly rejoiced and fully produced every edict received since the Zhenguan era to show Weiming.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan king was overjoyed and produced every imperial edict received since the Zhenguan reign to show Weiming.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，遣其大臣論名悉獵隨惟明入貢，表稱：「甥世尚公主，義同一家。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, he sent his great minister Lun Mingxilie to follow Weiming in presenting tribute; the memorial stated: "Your nephew has long honored the princess—the bond is as one family.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, he sent his minister Lun Mingxilie to accompany Weiming in tribute, writing: "Your nephew has long been married to the princess; we are kin as one household.

sentences.zh: 中間張玄表等先興兵寇鈔，遂使二境交惡。

translations.literal: In between Zhang Xuanbiao and others first raised troops to raid and plunder, thereby causing the two realms to turn mutually hostile.
translations.idiomatic: In the meantime Zhang Xuanbiao and others took the offensive, raiding across the border until both realms became sworn enemies.

sentences.zh: 甥深識尊卑，安敢失禮！

translations.literal: Your nephew deeply understands high and low—how dare he fail in ritual propriety!
translations.idiomatic: Your nephew knows well his place in the hierarchy—how could he breach decorum!

sentences.zh: 正為邊將交構，致獲罪於舅；

translations.literal: It is precisely because frontier generals sowed discord that he incurred guilt before his uncle-by-marriage;
translations.idiomatic: It was only because frontier generals stirred up trouble that I fell under my uncle's displeasure;

sentences.zh: 屢遣使者入朝，皆為邊將所遏。

translations.literal: Repeatedly dispatching envoys to court, all were obstructed by frontier generals.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again I sent envoys to court, but frontier generals blocked them every time.

sentences.zh: 今蒙遠降使臣，來視公主，甥不勝喜荷。

translations.literal: Now receiving from afar the descent of envoys to come view the princess, your nephew cannot bear the weight of joy and gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty has graciously sent envoys from afar to visit the princess, your nephew is overcome with joy and gratitude.

sentences.zh: 倘使復修舊好，死無所恨！」

translations.literal: If only the old good relations may be restored, in death there would be no regret!"
translations.idiomatic: If we can restore our former friendship, I shall die without regret!"

sentences.zh: 自是吐蕃復款附。

translations.literal: From this Tibet again submitted sincerely and attached itself.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Tibet renewed its loyal submission.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，上幸鳳泉湯；

translations.literal: On gengyin, the emperor visited Fengquan Hot Springs;
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the emperor traveled to the Fengquan hot springs;

sentences.zh: 癸卯，還京師。

translations.literal: On guimao, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, he came back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，護密王羅真檀入朝，留宿衛。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the king of Humu Luozhentan entered court and was retained for palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, King Luozhentan of Humu came to court and was kept on as an imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁卯，上幸驪山溫泉；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingmao, the emperor visited Mount Li Hot Springs;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingmao, the emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 丁丑，還宮。

translations.literal: On dingchou, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, he went back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下奏死罪止二十四人。

translations.literal: That year, empire-wide reports of capital punishment totaled only twenty-four persons.
translations.idiomatic: That year, capital sentences reported empire-wide numbered only twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 突騎施遣使入貢，上宴之於丹鳳樓，突厥使者預焉。

translations.literal: Turgesh dispatched envoys to present tribute; the emperor feasted them at Danfeng Tower, with Turkic envoys participating.
translations.idiomatic: Turgesh sent envoys with tribute, and the emperor held a banquet for them at Danfeng Tower, with Turkic envoys also in attendance.

sentences.zh: 二使爭長，突厥曰：「突騎施小國，本突厥之臣，不可居我上。」

translations.literal: The two envoys contended for precedence; the Turks said: "Turgesh is a small state, originally subject to the Turks—it cannot sit above us."
translations.idiomatic: The two delegations quarreled over precedence; the Turks said, "Turgesh is a petty realm, originally a Turkic vassal—it cannot sit above us."

sentences.zh: 突騎施曰：「今日之宴，為我設也，我不可以居其下。」

translations.literal: Turgesh said: "Today's banquet was set up for us—we cannot sit below them."
translations.idiomatic: Turgesh replied, "Today's feast was held for us—we will not take a lower seat."

sentences.zh: 上乃命設東、西幕，突厥在東，突騎施在西。

translations.literal: The emperor then commanded east and west tents to be set up—the Turks in the east, Turgesh in the west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had two tents erected—Turks to the east, Turgesh to the west.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司、內外閒廄監牧都使霍國公王毛仲恃寵，驕恣日甚，上每優容之。

translations.literal: Wang Maochong, Duke of Huo, Grandee of Splendid Happiness with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and Chief Controller of Palace and Outer Stud Pastures, relied on favor; arrogance and license grew daily severer, and the emperor always treated him with exceptional forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maochong, Duke of Huo—Grandee of Splendid Happiness and chief of the imperial stud—grew ever more arrogant on imperial favor, yet the emperor indulged him at every turn.

sentences.zh: 毛仲與左領軍大將軍葛福順、左監門將軍唐地文、左武衛將軍李守德、右威衛將軍王景耀、高廣濟親善，福順等倚其勢，多為不法。

translations.literal: Maochong was intimate with Left Vanguard Army Grand General Ge Fushun, Left Gate Guard General Tang Diwen, Left Martial Guard General Li Shoude, Right Majestic Guard General Wang Jingyao, and Gao Guangji; Fushun and the others relied on his power and frequently acted against law.
translations.idiomatic: Maochong was close to Left Vanguard commander Ge Fushun, Left Gate Guard general Tang Diwen, Left Martial Guard general Li Shoude, Right Majestic Guard general Wang Jingyao, and Gao Guangji; Fushun and the others traded on his power and broke the law with impunity.

sentences.zh: 毛仲求兵部尚書不得，怏怏形於辭色，上由是不悅。

translations.literal: Maochong sought Minister of War and did not obtain it; displeasure showed in word and countenance, and the emperor from this was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Maochong asked for the post of Minister of War and was refused; his resentment showed plainly in speech and face, and the emperor took displeasure at it.

sentences.zh: 是時，上頗寵任宦官，往往為三品將軍，門施棨戟；

translations.literal: At this time the emperor quite favored and employed eunuchs, who often held third-rank generalships, their gates bearing ceremonial halberds;
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor favored eunuchs heavily, often promoting them to third-rank generals with ceremonial halberds displayed at their gates;

sentences.zh: 奉使過諸州，官吏奉之惟恐不及，所得賂遺，少者不減千緡；

translations.literal: When sent on missions passing through the provinces, officials waited on them fearing they might fall short; bribes and gifts received—at the least not less than a thousand strings;
translations.idiomatic: On missions through the provinces, officials fawned on them for fear of giving offense, and the bribes they collected never fell below a thousand strings of cash;

sentences.zh: 由是京城第捨、郊畿田園，參半皆宦官矣。

translations.literal: From this the mansions in the capital and suburban fields and gardens were half and more all eunuchs'.
translations.idiomatic: So that half the mansions in the capital and half the estates in the suburbs passed into eunuch hands.

sentences.zh: 楊思勖、高力士尤貴幸，思勖屢將兵征討，力士常居中侍衛。

translations.literal: Yang Sixu and Gao Lishi were especially honored and favored; Sixu repeatedly led troops on punitive campaigns, Lishi constantly attended within as bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sixu and Gao Lishi were the most exalted among them—Sixu often led armies on campaign, while Lishi usually stayed at court as personal guard.

sentences.zh: 而毛仲視宦官貴近者若無人；

translations.literal: Yet Maochong viewed eminent and near eunuchs as though no one were there;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Maochong treated even the most powerful eunuchs as beneath notice;

sentences.zh: 甚卑品者，小忤意，輒詈辱如僮僕。

translations.literal: Those of very low rank, if they slightly offended his intent, he would immediately revile and humiliate like house boys.
translations.idiomatic: And if the lowliest among them gave the slightest offense, he would berate and humiliate them like household servants.

sentences.zh: 力士等皆害其寵而未敢言。

translations.literal: Lishi and the others all resented his favor yet did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi and the others resented his favor but dared not speak out.

sentences.zh: 會毛仲妻產子，三日，上命力士賜之酒饌、金帛甚厚，且授其兒五品官。

translations.literal: It happened that Maochong's wife bore a child; on the third day the emperor commanded Lishi to bestow wine, food, gold, and silk in great abundance, and moreover grant his son a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: When Maochong's wife gave birth, on the third day the emperor sent Lishi with lavish gifts of wine, food, gold, and silk—and granted the newborn a fifth-rank office.

sentences.zh: 力士還，上問：「毛仲喜乎？」

translations.literal: Lishi returned; the emperor asked: "Is Maochong pleased?"
translations.idiomatic: When Lishi returned, the emperor asked, "Was Maochong pleased?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「毛仲抱其襁中兒示臣曰：『此兒豈不堪作三品邪！』」

translations.literal: He replied: "Maochong held his infant in swaddling clothes and showed me, saying: 'Is this child not fit to be made third rank!'"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Maochong held up his swaddled infant and said to me, 'Surely this boy deserves a third-rank post!'"

sentences.zh: 上大怒曰：「昔誅韋氏，此賊心持兩端，朕不欲言之；

translations.literal: The emperor greatly raged and said: "In the past when the Wei clan was executed, this traitor's heart wavered between two sides—I did not wish to speak of it;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage. "When the Wei clan was destroyed, this villain hedged his loyalty—I held my tongue then;

sentences.zh: 今日乃敢以赤子怨我！」

translations.literal: Today he dares use a newborn to resent me!"
translations.idiomatic: Now he dares flaunt his infant to show his resentment!"

sentences.zh: 力士因言：「北門奴，官太盛，相與一心，不早除之，必生大患！」

translations.literal: Lishi thereupon said: "The North Gate slaves—their offices too flourishing, united as one heart—if not removed early, great calamity will surely arise!"
translations.idiomatic: Lishi then said, "These North Gate slaves hold too much power and act as one bloc—unless they are cut down soon, they will bring great disaster!"

sentences.zh: 上恐其黨驚懼為變。

translations.literal: The emperor feared their faction, alarmed, might rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared that if their faction panicked, they might rise in revolt.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬戌，下制，但述毛仲不忠怨望，貶瀼州別駕，福順、地文、守德、景耀、廣濟皆貶遠州別駕，毛仲四子皆貶遠州參軍，連坐者數十人。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renxu, an edict was issued stating only that Maochong was disloyal and resentful, demoting him to assistant prefect of Rang; Fushun, Diwen, Shoude, Jingyao, and Guangji were all demoted to assistant prefects of distant prefectures; Maochong's four sons were all demoted to military adjutants of distant prefectures; those implicated numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renxu, an edict was promulgated citing only Maochong's disloyalty and resentment—he was demoted to assistant prefect of Rang; Fushun, Diwen, Shoude, Jingyao, and Guangji were banished to distant prefectures as assistant prefects; Maochong's four sons were reduced to military adjutants in remote posts; dozens were implicated.

sentences.zh: 毛仲行至永州，追賜死。

translations.literal: Maochong traveled as far as Yongzhou; he was overtaken and granted death by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Maochong had reached Yongzhou when an imperial messenger overtook him and ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 自是宦官勢益盛。

translations.literal: From this the power of eunuchs grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: From then on eunuch power swelled still further.

sentences.zh: 高力士尤為上所寵信，嘗曰：「力士上直，吾寢則安。」

translations.literal: Gao Lishi was especially trusted and favored by the emperor; he once said: "When Lishi is on duty above, my sleep is then peaceful."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi enjoyed the emperor's special trust; the emperor once said, "When Lishi is on duty, I sleep soundly."

sentences.zh: 故力士多留禁中，稀至外第。

translations.literal: Therefore Lishi often remained within the forbidden precincts and rarely went to his outer residence.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Lishi spent most of his time inside the palace and seldom visited his private residence.

sentences.zh: 四方表奏，皆先呈力士，然後奏御；

translations.literal: Memorials from the four directions all were first presented to Lishi, then submitted to the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Petitions from across the realm were routed first to Lishi and only then forwarded to the emperor;

sentences.zh: 事小者力士即決之，勢傾內外。

translations.literal: On small matters Lishi decided them immediately; his power leaned against inner and outer alike.
translations.idiomatic: Trivial matters Lishi decided on the spot—and his influence eclipsed court and government alike.

sentences.zh: 金吾大將軍程伯獻、少府監馮紹正與力士約為兄弟；

translations.literal: Cavalry Guard Grand General Cheng Boxian and Court of Palace Supplies Director Feng Shaozheng with Lishi pledged themselves as sworn brothers;
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry Guard commander Cheng Boxian and Court of Palace Supplies director Feng Shaozheng swore brotherhood with Lishi;

sentences.zh: 力士母麥氏卒，伯獻等被發受吊，擗踴哭泣，過於己親。

translations.literal: When Lishi's mother Lady Mai died, Boxian and the others disheveled their hair to receive condolences, beating their breasts and weeping—more than for their own kin.
translations.idiomatic: And when Lishi's mother Lady Mai died, Boxian and the others came with hair unbound to mourn, wailing and beating their breasts more fervently than at their own parents' funerals.

sentences.zh: 力士娶瀛州呂玄晤女為妻，擢玄晤為少卿，子弟皆王傅。

translations.literal: Lishi took as wife the daughter of Lü Xuanwu of Yingzhou; Xuanwu was elevated to Vice Director, and his sons and younger brothers all became princes' tutors.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi married the daughter of Lü Xuanwu of Yingzhou; Xuanwu was promoted to vice director, and his sons and nephews all became tutors to imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 呂氏卒，朝野爭致祭，自第至墓，車馬不絕。

translations.literal: When Lady Lü died, court and countryside vied to offer sacrifice; from mansion to tomb, chariots and horses without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Lü died, officials and commoners competed to send offerings, and carriages jammed the road from her home to the grave.

sentences.zh: 然力士小心恭恪，故上終親任之。

translations.literal: Yet Lishi was careful, respectful, and reverent, and therefore the emperor to the end personally trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lishi remained discreet and deferential, and so the emperor continued to rely on him to the end.

sentences.zh: 辛未，遣鴻臚卿崔琳使於吐蕃。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Minister of Ceremonies Cui Lin was dispatched as envoy to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the Minister of Ceremonies Cui Lin was sent as envoy to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 琳，神慶之子也。

translations.literal: Lin was the son of Shenqing.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lin was the son of Cui Shenqing.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃使者稱公主求《毛詩》、《春秋》、《禮記》。

translations.literal: The Tibetan envoy stated the princess sought the Mao Odes, the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the Book of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan envoy reported that the princess had requested the Mao Odes, the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 正字於休烈上疏，以為：「東平王漢之懿親，求《史記》、《諸子》，漢猶不與。

translations.literal: Secretariat Reviser Yu Xiulie submitted a memorial, holding: "Prince Dongping, Han's close imperial kinsman, sought the Records of the Grand Historian and the Masters texts—Han still did not grant them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiulie, a reviser in the Secretariat, memorialized: "When Prince Dongping, a close Han imperial relative, asked for the Records of the Grand Historian and the Masters texts, even Han refused.

sentences.zh: 況吐蕃，國之寇仇，今資之以書，使知用兵權略，愈生變詐，非中國之利也。」

translations.literal: How much more Tibet, the state's enemy and foe—now supplying them with books, causing them to know military deployment, stratagem, and trickery, further giving rise to change and fraud—this is not China's profit."
translations.idiomatic: How much less should we arm Tibet, a sworn enemy of the realm, with books that teach the arts of war and stratagem—they will only grow more cunning and treacherous, to China's harm."

sentences.zh: 事下中書門下議之。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Secretariat and Chancellery to deliberate it.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Secretariat and Chancellery for discussion.

sentences.zh: 裴光庭等奏：「吐蕃聾昧頑嚚，久叛新服，因其有請，賜以《詩》、《書》，庶使之漸陶聲教，化流無外。

translations.literal: Pei Guangting and others memorialized: "Tibet is deaf, dim, stubborn, and brutish—long in rebellion, newly submissive; because they have a request, bestow upon them the Odes and the Documents, hoping thereby to gradually immerse them in our civilizing influence, transforming flow without bound.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Guangting and others replied: "Tibet is stubborn and uncivilized—long rebellious, newly subdued. Since they ask, grant them the Odes and the Documents, that they may gradually absorb our culture until civilization reaches beyond our borders.

sentences.zh: 休烈徒知書有權略變詐之語，不知忠、信、禮、義，皆從書出也。」

translations.literal: Xiulie knows only that books contain language of stratagem and fraudulent change, and does not know that loyalty, faith, ritual, and righteousness all emerge from books."
translations.idiomatic: Xiulie sees only the passages on stratagem and deceit, and fails to see that loyalty, faith, ritual, and righteousness—all come from those same books."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 遂與之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were granted to them.
translations.idiomatic: The texts were duly granted.

sentences.zh: 休烈，志寧之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Xiulie was the great-great-grandson of Zhenning.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiulie was the great-great-grandson of Yu Zhenning.

sentences.zh: 丙子，上躬耕於興慶宮側，盡三百步。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the emperor personally plowed beside Xingqing Palace, completing three hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, the emperor personally farmed beside Xingqing Palace, completing the full three hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 三月，突厥左賢王闕特勒卒，賜書吊之。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Turkic Left Wise Prince Qie Teller died; an imperial letter was bestowed to condole.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the Turkic Left Wise Prince Qie Teller died, and the emperor sent a letter of condolence.

sentences.zh: 丙申，初令兩京諸州各置太公廟，以張良配饗，選古名將，以備十哲；

translations.literal: On bingshen, for the first time both capitals and all prefectures were each ordered to establish a Grand Duke Temple, with Zhang Liang as associate sacrifice, selecting ancient famed generals to complete the Ten Worthies;
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, temples to the Grand Duke were established in both capitals and every prefecture for the first time, with Zhang Liang enshrined as his associate and ancient famous generals chosen to fill out the Ten Worthies;

sentences.zh: 以二、八月上戊致祭，如孔子禮。

translations.literal: On the upper wu days of the second and eighth months sacrifice was performed, as with Confucius's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices were scheduled for the first wu days of the second and eighth months, following the ritual pattern used for Confucius.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：經緯天地之謂文，戡定禍亂之謂武。

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: Ordering heaven and earth is called wen; pacifying and settling calamity and disorder is called wu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: To array heaven and earth is called cultural virtue; to suppress chaos and restore order is called martial virtue.

sentences.zh: 自古不兼斯二者而稱聖人，未之有也。

translations.literal: From antiquity no one who did not combine these two and yet was called sage—never has there been such.
translations.idiomatic: Never in history has anyone been called a sage who lacked both.

sentences.zh: 故黃帝、堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武、伊尹、周公莫不有征伐之功，孔子雖不試，猶能兵萊夷，卻費人，曰：「吾戰則克」，豈孔子專文而太公專武乎？

translations.literal: Therefore the Yellow Emperor, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, Yi Yin, and Duke of Zhou—none lacked the achievement of punitive campaigns; Confucius though not employed still could take arms against the Yi of Lai, repel the people of Fei, and say: "If I fight, then I conquer"—how could Confucius be exclusively wen and the Grand Duke exclusively wu?
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, King Wu, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou all won victories in war; Confucius, though never given office, still subdued the Yi of Lai, drove back the people of Fei, and declared, "If I fight, I conquer"—was Confucius purely a man of culture and the Grand Duke purely a man of war?

sentences.zh: 孔子所以祀於學者，禮有先聖先師故也。

translations.literal: The reason Confucius is sacrificed to in the school is that ritual has First Sage and First Master, therefore.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius is honored in the academy because ritual tradition designates a First Sage and First Master.

sentences.zh: 自生民以來，未有如孔子者，豈太公得與之抗衡哉！

translations.literal: From the living people down to the present, none like Confucius—how could the Grand Duke measure against him in contention!
translations.idiomatic: Since the dawn of humanity there has been no one like Confucius—how could the Grand Duke stand as his rival!

sentences.zh: 古者有發，則命大司徒教士以車甲，臝股肱，決射御，受成獻馘，莫不在學。

translations.literal: In antiquity when there was mobilization, then the Grand Minister of Education was commanded to teach scholars with chariots and armor, bare the arms and legs, decide archery and charioteering, receive completion and present severed ears—all not outside the school.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when war was declared, the Grand Minister of Education trained scholars in chariots and armor, bared their limbs for drill, tested archery and charioteering, and received battle reports and severed ears—all within the academy.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，欲其先禮義而後勇力也。

translations.literal: The reason for this was to desire that they put ritual and righteousness first and courage and strength after.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was to instill ritual and righteousness before raw courage and brute strength.

sentences.zh: 君子有勇而無義為亂，小人有勇而無義為盜；

translations.literal: The noble man with courage yet without righteousness becomes disorder; the petty man with courage yet without righteousness becomes a thief;
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman with courage but no sense of right breeds rebellion; a commoner with courage but no sense of right becomes a bandit;

sentences.zh: 若專訓之以勇力而不使之知禮義，奚所不為矣！

translations.literal: If one exclusively trains them in courage and strength yet does not cause them to know ritual and righteousness, what would they not do!
translations.idiomatic: Train men only in brute force without teaching them propriety, and there is no atrocity they will not commit!

sentences.zh: 自孫、吳以降，皆為勇力相勝，狙詐相高，豈足以數於聖賢之門而謂之武哉！

translations.literal: From Sun and Wu downward, all are those in whom courage and strength mutually overcome, furtive trickery mutually exalted—how could they be counted in the gate of sages and worthies and called wu!
translations.idiomatic: From Sun Tzu and Wu Qi onward, martial fame has rested on brute strength and cunning stratagem—what has that to do with the martial virtue of the sages!

sentences.zh: 乃復誣引以偶十哲之目，為後世學者之師；

translations.literal: Yet again falsely citing them to pair with the roster of Ten Worthies, making them teachers for scholars of later ages;
translations.idiomatic: To drag such men into the Ten Worthies and set them up as models for future generations—

sentences.zh: 使太公有神，必羞與之同食矣！

translations.literal: If the Grand Duke had a spirit, he would surely be ashamed to eat sacrifice with them!
translations.idiomatic: If the Grand Duke's spirit were present, he would be ashamed to share the sacrificial feast with them!

sentences.zh: 五月，壬戌，初立五嶽真君祠。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renxu, for the first time shrines to the True Lords of the Five Sacred Peaks were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renxu, temples to the True Lords of the Five Sacred Peaks were established for the first time.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，辛未，吐蕃遣其相論尚它硉入見，請於赤嶺為互市；

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on xinwei, Tibet sent its chancellor Lun Shang Taliu to enter audience, requesting at Chiling a mutual market;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, on xinwei, Tibet sent Chancellor Lun Shang Taliu to court, requesting a border market at Chiling;

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙申，上幸東都。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingshen, the emperor visited the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingshen, the emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 或告巂州都督解人張審素贓污，制遣監察御史楊汪按之。

translations.literal: Someone reported the Governor of Xi Prefecture, Zhang Shenjie of Jie, for corruption and defilement; by edict Supervising Censor Yang Wang was dispatched to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Someone denounced Zhang Shenjie of Jie, military governor of Xi Prefecture, for corruption, and an edict sent Supervising Censor Yang Wang to investigate.

sentences.zh: 總管董元禮將兵七百圍汪，殺告者，謂汪曰：「善奏審素則生，不然則死。」

translations.literal: Commandant Dong Yuanli led seven hundred troops to surround Wang, killed the accuser, and said to Wang: "Report Shenjie favorably and you live; otherwise you die."
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Dong Yuanli marched seven hundred men to surround Wang, killed the informant, and told Wang, "File a favorable report on Shenjie and you live—otherwise you die."

sentences.zh: 會救兵至，擊斬之。

translations.literal: It happened that relief troops arrived and struck, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops arrived in time and killed Yuanli in the attack.

sentences.zh: 汪奏審素謀反，十二月，癸未，審素坐斬，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Wang memorialized that Shenjie plotted rebellion; in the twelfth month, on guiwei, Shenjie was executed by sitting judgment, and his household was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Wang reported that Shenjie had plotted rebellion; in the twelfth month, on guiwei, Shenjie was beheaded and his property seized.

sentences.zh: 浚苑中洛水，六旬而罷。

translations.literal: The Luo River within the imperial park was dredged—for sixty days then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Luo River in the imperial park was dredged—a project that ran sixty days before it was halted.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙卯，以朔方節度副大使信安王禕為河東、河北行軍副大總管，將兵擊奚、契丹；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yimao, Prince Xin'an Yi, Vice Commissioner of the Shuofang Military Commission, was made Vice Grand Commander of the Hedong and Hebei field armies, leading troops to strike the Xi and Khitan;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yimao, Prince Xin'an Yi, deputy commissioner of Shuofang, was appointed deputy grand commander of the Hedong and Hebei field armies to lead troops against the Xi and Khitan;

sentences.zh: 壬申，以戶部侍郎裴耀卿為副總管。

translations.literal: On renshen, Vice Minister of Revenue Pei Yaojing was made deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Vice Minister of Revenue Pei Yaojing was appointed deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the guiyou new moon, the sun had an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, at the guiyou new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 上思右驍衛將軍安金藏忠烈，三月，賜爵代國公，仍於東、西嶽立碑，以銘其功。

translations.literal: The emperor recalled Right Valiant Cavalry General An Jincang's loyal martyrdom; in the third month, he bestowed on him the title Duke of Dai, and furthermore had steles erected at the Eastern and Western Peaks to inscribe his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Right Valiant Cavalry General An Jincang's fearless loyalty, the emperor in the third month ennobled him as Duke of Dai and ordered steles raised on the Eastern and Western Sacred Peaks to commemorate his service.

sentences.zh: 金藏竟以壽終。

translations.literal: Jincang in the end died of old age.
translations.idiomatic: An Jincang lived out his years and died a natural death.

sentences.zh: 信安王禕帥裴耀卿及幽州節度使趙含章分道擊奚、契丹，含章與虜遇，虜望風遁去。

translations.literal: Prince Xin'an Yi led Pei Yaojing and Youzhou Military Commissioner Zhao Hanzhang on separate routes to strike the Xi and Khitan; Hanzhang encountered the barbarians, and the barbarians at sight of the wind fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin'an Yi, commanding Pei Yaojing and Youzhou commissioner Zhao Hanzhang, attacked the Xi and Khitan on separate fronts; when Zhao Hanzhang met the enemy, they fled at the first sign of his approach.

sentences.zh: 平盧先鋒將烏承禕言於含章曰：「二虜，劇賊也。

translations.literal: Pinglu vanguard general Wu Chengyi said to Hanzhang: "The two barbarians are fierce bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Pinglu vanguard Wu Chengyi warned Hanzhang: "These two peoples are ruthless foes.

sentences.zh: 前日遁去，非畏我，乃誘我也，宜按兵以觀其變。」

translations.literal: Yesterday's fleeing away was not fearing us—it was luring us; one should hold the army to observe their change."
translations.idiomatic: Their retreat the other day was not cowardice but bait; we should hold our troops back and watch how matters develop."

sentences.zh: 含章不從，與虜戰於白山，果大敗。

translations.literal: Hanzhang did not follow; he fought the barbarians at White Mountain, and indeed suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhang ignored the advice, engaged the enemy at White Mountain, and was routed.

sentences.zh: 承玼引兵出其右，擊虜，破之。

translations.literal: Chengyi led troops out from their right flank, struck the barbarians, and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengyi swung his force around the enemy's right, attacked, and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 己巳，禕等大破奚、契丹，俘斬甚眾，可突干帥麾下遠遁，餘黨潛竄山谷。

translations.literal: On jisi, Yi and the others greatly defeated the Xi and Khitan, capturing and slaying very many; Ketugan led his personal followers in distant flight, and the remaining factions secretly fled into mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Yi won a crushing victory over the Xi and Khitan, taking and killing a great multitude; Ketugan fled far away with his personal following while the rest scattered into the hills.

sentences.zh: 奚酉李詩瑣高帥五千餘帳來降。

translations.literal: Xi chieftain Li Shisuogao led more than five thousand households in coming to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shisuogao, a Xi chieftain, submitted with more than five thousand tents.

sentences.zh: 禕引兵還。

translations.literal: Yi led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Yi withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 賜李詩爵歸義王，充歸義州都督，徒其部落置幽州境內。

translations.literal: Li Shi was granted the title Prince Who Returns to Righteousness, appointed military commissioner of Guyi Prefecture, and his tribal group was moved and placed within Youzhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi was made Prince of Returning Allegiance, named commissioner of Guyi Prefecture, and his people were resettled within Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙亥，宴百官於上陽東洲，醉者賜以衾褥，肩輿以歸，相屬於路。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yihai, he feasted the hundred officials at Shangyang's East Islet; the drunk were given quilts and bedding, carried on palanquins to return, one after another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yihai, the emperor entertained the whole court on the eastern islet of Shangyang Palace; officials who drank too much were given bedding and sent home in sedan chairs, a procession stretching along the road.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁丑，加信安王禕開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingchou, Prince Xin'an Yi was additionally given Opens an Office with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingchou, Prince Xin'an Yi was granted the rank of Grand Generalissimo with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 上命裴耀卿繼絹二十萬匹分賜立功奚官，耀卿謂其徒曰：「戎狄貪婪，今繼重貨深入其境，不可不備。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Pei Yaojing to follow with two hundred thousand bolts of silk to distribute in rewarding meritorious Xi officials; Yaojing said to his followers: "The Rong and Di are greedy; now following heavy goods deep into their territory—one cannot fail to take precautions."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor charged Pei Yaojing to deliver two hundred thousand bolts of silk as rewards for Xi officers who had distinguished themselves; Yaojing told his staff, "These tribes are rapacious; carrying such treasure deep into their lands demands every precaution."

sentences.zh: 乃命先期而往，分道並進，一日，給之俱畢。

translations.literal: He then ordered going ahead of schedule, advancing by separate routes together; in one day, distributing them all was completed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the goods ahead on several routes at once and distributed the entire allotment in a single day.

sentences.zh: 突厥、室韋果發兵邀隘道，欲掠之，比至，耀卿已還。

translations.literal: The Turks and Shiwei indeed dispatched troops to intercept the narrow passes, intending to plunder them; by the time they arrived, Yaojing had already returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks and Shiwei did marshal forces to ambush the mountain passes and seize the silk, but by the time they arrived Yaojing was already gone.

sentences.zh: 趙含章坐贓巨萬，杖於朝堂，流瀼州，道死。

translations.literal: Zhao Hanzhang sat guilty of embezzlement of tens of thousands; he was beaten at the court hall, exiled to Rang Prefecture, and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hanzhang was convicted of taking bribes worth tens of thousands of strings of cash; he was flogged in the imperial hall, banished to Rang Prefecture, and died en route.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，蕭嵩奏：「自祠后土以來，屢獲豐年，宜因還京賽祠。」

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Xiao Song memorialized: "Since sacrificing to the Earth Sovereign, repeatedly obtaining bountiful years—it is fitting, upon returning to the capital, to hold a thanksgiving sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Xiao Song urged, "Ever since the rites to the Earth Sovereign, harvests have repeatedly been abundant; we should offer a thanksgiving sacrifice when we return to the capital."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 敕裴光庭、蕭嵩分押左、右廂兵。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Pei Guangting and Xiao Song separately to oversee the left and right wing troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Pei Guangting and Xiao Song each to command the left and right palace guard divisions.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the xinwei new moon, the sun had an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, at the xinwei new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 初，上命張說與諸學士刊定五禮。

translations.literal: Initially, the emperor ordered Zhang Yue and the various academicians to revise and fix the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor had charged Zhang Yue and the palace academicians with compiling the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 說薨，蕭嵩繼之。

translations.literal: Yue died; Xiao Song succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue died, Xiao Song took over the project.

sentences.zh: 起居舍人王仲丘請依《明慶禮》，祈谷、大雩、明堂，皆祀昊天上帝；

translations.literal: Diarist Wang Zhongqiu requested following the Mingqing Rites—that at Prayers for Grain, the Great Rain Rite, and the Bright Hall, all should sacrifice to the Grand August Heaven Thearch;
translations.idiomatic: Court diarist Wang Zhongqiu proposed adopting the Mingqing Rites so that the rites of Praying for Grain, the Great Yu, and the Bright Hall would all honor the Supreme Deity of Heaven;

sentences.zh: 嵩又請依上元敕，父在為母齊衰三年。

translations.literal: Song again requested following the Shangyuan edict—that with the father living, one wears unhemmed hemp mourning for the mother for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Song also asked that mourning rules follow the Shangyuan edict, requiring three years of hemp mourning for a mother while the father still lived.

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved both proposals.

sentences.zh: 以高祖配圜丘、方丘，太宗配雩祀及神州地祇，睿宗配明堂。

translations.literal: Gaozu was paired at the Round Mound and Square Mound; Taizong was paired at the rain rite and the Spirit of the Land within the Realm; Ruizong was paired at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was made associate spirit at the Round and Square Altars; Emperor Taizong at the rain sacrifice and the altar of the land; Emperor Ruizong at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙巳，新禮成，上之，號曰《開元禮》。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yisi, the new rites were completed, submitted upward, and titled the Kaiyuan Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yisi, the new code was finished, presented to the throne, and named the Kaiyuan Rites.

sentences.zh: 勃海靺鞨王武藝遣其將張文休帥海賊寇登州，殺刺史韋俊，上命右領軍將軍葛福順發兵討之。

translations.literal: Bohai Mohe King Wuyi sent his general Zhang Wenxiu leading sea bandits to raid Deng Prefecture, killing Prefect Wei Jun; the emperor ordered Right Vanguard General Ge Fushun to dispatch troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi, king of Bohai Mohe, sent his general Zhang Wenxiu at the head of pirates to attack Deng Prefecture and kill its prefect Wei Jun; the emperor ordered Right Vanguard General Ge Fushun to lead a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 壬子，河西節度使牛仙客加六階。

translations.literal: On renzi, Hexi Military Commissioner Niu Xianke was advanced six ranks.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Hexi commissioner Niu Xianke was promoted six grades.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭嵩在河西，委軍政於仙客；

translations.literal: Initially, when Xiao Song was in Hexi, he entrusted military and civil affairs to Xianke;
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Song held the Hexi command, he had entrusted civil and military affairs to Niu Xianke;

sentences.zh: 仙客廉勤，善於其職。

translations.literal: Xianke was incorrupt and diligent, good at his post.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Xianke was honest and industrious and excelled in the role.

sentences.zh: 嵩屢薦之，竟代嵩為節度使。

translations.literal: Song repeatedly recommended him; in the end he replaced Song as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Song recommended him again and again, and Niu Xianke eventually succeeded him as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬午，上發東都；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renwu, the emperor departed the Eastern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on renwu, the emperor left Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，幸潞州；

translations.literal: On xinmao, he visited Lu Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao he traveled to Lu Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 辛丑，至北都；

translations.literal: On xinchou, he arrived at the Northern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou he reached Taiyuan;

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚申，祀后土於汾陰，赦天下；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengshen, he sacrificed to the Earth Sovereign at Fenyin, and pardoned all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengshen, he performed the rite to the Earth Sovereign at Fenyin and proclaimed a general amnesty;

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛未，還西京。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on xinwei, he returned to the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinwei, he returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以幽州節度使兼河北採訪處置使增領衛、相、洛、貝、冀、魏、深、趙、恆、定、邢、德、博、棣、營、鄚十六州及安東都護府。

translations.literal: That year, the Youzhou Military Commissioner concurrently Hebei Investigation and Disposition Commissioner additionally superintended Wei, Xiang, Luo, Bei, Ji, Wei, Shen, Zhao, Heng, Ding, Xing, De, Bo, Di, Ying, and Mao—sixteen prefectures—and the Protectorate General of Andong.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Youzhou commissioner, who also served as Hebei investigation commissioner, was given authority over sixteen prefectures—Wei, Xiang, Luo, Bei, Ji, Wei, Shen, Zhao, Heng, Ding, Xing, De, Bo, Di, Ying, and Mao—as well as the Protectorate General of Andong.

sentences.zh: 天下戶七百八十六萬一千二百三十六，口四千五百四十三萬一千二百六十五。

translations.literal: All under Heaven: households seven million eight hundred sixty-one thousand two hundred thirty-six; mouths forty-five million four hundred thirty-one thousand two hundred sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: The empire registered 7,861,236 households and a population of 45,431,265.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙巳，祔肅明皇后於太廟，毀儀坤廟。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yisi, Empress Sumei was enshrined alongside in the Grand Temple; the Yikun Temple was demolished.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yisi, Empress Sumei was given a place in the imperial ancestral temple and the separate Yikun shrine was abolished.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，上幸驪山溫泉。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the emperor visited Mount Li Hot Springs.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 上遣大門藝詣幽州發兵，以討勃海王武藝；

translations.literal: The emperor sent Dae Mun-ye to You Prefecture to raise troops, to suppress Bohai King Wuyi;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Dae Mun-ye to Youzhou to mobilize troops against Wuyi of Bohai;

sentences.zh: 庚申，命太僕員外卿金思蘭使於新羅，發兵擊其南鄙。

translations.literal: On gengshen, he ordered Vice Master of Horse Jin Silan as envoy to Silla, to raise troops and strike its southern borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he sent Vice Master of Horse Jin Silan to Silla to muster forces for an attack on Bohai's southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 會大雪丈餘，山路阻隘，士卒死者過半，無功而還。

translations.literal: Meeting with heavy snow more than a zhang deep, mountain roads blocked and narrow, soldiers dying over half; without achievement they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Snow piled more than ten feet deep, blocking the mountain passes; more than half the troops perished, and the expedition returned empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 武藝怨門藝不已，密遣客刺門藝於天津橋南，不死；

translations.literal: Wuyi bore a grudge against Mun-ye without end, secretly sending a guest to assassinate Mun-ye south of the Tianjin Bridge; he did not die;
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi nursed a deep grievance against Dae Mun-ye and secretly sent an agent to stab him south of the Tianjin Bridge, but Mun-ye survived;

sentences.zh: 上命河南搜捕賊黨，盡殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Henan to search and seize the bandit faction; all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Henan to hunt down the assassins and had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁酉，金城公主請立碑於赤嶺以分唐與吐蕃之境；

translations.literal: In the second month, on dingyou, Princess Jincheng requested erecting a stele at Red Ridge to divide Tang and Tubo's border;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingyou, Princess Jincheng asked that a boundary stele be erected at Red Ridge to mark the border between Tang and Tibet;

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙巳，侍中裴光庭薨。

translations.literal: In the third month, on yisi, Palace Attendant Pei Guangting died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yisi, Chief Minister Pei Guangting died.

sentences.zh: 太常博士孫琬議：「光庭用循資格，失勸獎之道，請謚曰克。」

translations.literal: Grand Ritual Specialist Sun Wan proposed: "Guangting employed following seniority ranks, losing the way of encouragement and reward; I request the posthumous title Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wan of the Grand Sacrificial Office argued, "Guangting rose by seniority alone and forfeited the principle of rewarding merit; I propose the posthumous name Ke ['Overcoming']."

sentences.zh: 其子稹訟之，上賜謚忠獻。

translations.literal: His son Zhen petitioned against it; the emperor bestowed the posthumous title Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pei Zhen appealed; the emperor granted the posthumous name Loyal and Dedicated.

sentences.zh: 上問蕭嵩可以代光庭者。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Xiao Song who could replace Guangting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Xiao Song whom he could appoint to succeed Pei Guangting.

sentences.zh: 嵩與右散騎常侍王丘善，將薦之；

translations.literal: Song was on good terms with Right Regular Palace Attendant Wang Qiu, and was about to recommend him;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Song was close to Right Palace Attendant Wang Qiu and meant to recommend him;

sentences.zh: 丘聞之，固讓於右丞韓休。

translations.literal: Qiu heard of it and firmly yielded to Right Vice Director Han Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qiu learned of this, he steadfastly declined in favor of Vice Director Han Xiu.

sentences.zh: 嵩言休於上。

translations.literal: Song spoke of Xiu to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Song then presented Han Xiu to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以休為黃門侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Xiu was made Yellow Gate Vice Minister and Participant in Equal Discussion of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Han Xiu was appointed Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 休為人峭直，不干榮利；

translations.literal: Xiu as a man was steep and straight, not meddling in glory and profit;
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu was stern and upright, indifferent to rank and gain;

sentences.zh: 及為相，甚允時望。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister, very much meeting the age's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: Once elevated to chief minister, he fully satisfied public expectations.

sentences.zh: 始，嵩以休恬和，謂其易制，故引之。

translations.literal: At first, Song regarded Xiu as tranquil and harmonious, thinking him easy to control—therefore brought him in.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Song had taken Xiu's mild manner for compliance and brought him in expecting an easy partner.

sentences.zh: 及與共事，休守正不阿，嵩漸惡之。

translations.literal: When they shared office together, Xiu upheld rectitude without bending; Song gradually hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Once they worked together, Han Xiu held to principle without yielding, and Xiao Song soon came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 宋璟歎曰：「不意韓休乃能如是！」

translations.literal: Song Jing sighed and said: "I did not expect Han Xiu could be thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing exclaimed, "Who would have thought Han Xiu capable of this!"

sentences.zh: 上或宮中宴樂及後苑遊獵，小有過差，輒謂左右曰：「韓休知否？」

translations.literal: The emperor occasionally at palace feasts and music or hunting in the rear park, with slight excesses, would at once say to those at hand: "Does Han Xiu know?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor indulged in palace revels or hunts in the imperial park, even in small lapses, he would turn to his attendants and ask, "Does Han Xiu know about this?"

sentences.zh: 言終，諫疏已至。

translations.literal: When the words ended, remonstrance memorials had already arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Barely had he spoken when a memorial of remonstrance would arrive.

sentences.zh: 上嘗臨鏡默然不樂，左右曰：「韓休為相，陛下殊瘦於舊，何不逐之！」

translations.literal: The emperor once faced the mirror silently unhappy; those at hand said: "With Han Xiu as chief minister, Your Majesty is especially thin compared with before—why not drive him out!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, gazing in the mirror in silent displeasure, his attendants said, "Since Han Xiu became chief minister Your Majesty has grown noticeably thinner—why not dismiss him!"

sentences.zh: 上歎曰：「吾貌雖瘦，天下必肥。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: "Though my appearance is thin, all under Heaven must be fat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed, "I may have grown thin, but the realm will prosper the more for it.

sentences.zh: 蕭嵩奏事常順指，既退，吾寢不安。

translations.literal: Xiao Song when memorializing affairs constantly followed the finger; once he withdrew, my sleep was not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Song reported to me he always told me what I wished to hear; once he left I could not sleep easy.

sentences.zh: 韓休常力爭，既退，吾寢乃安。

translations.literal: Han Xiu constantly strove with force; once he withdrew, my sleep then was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu always argued his case firmly; when he withdrew I slept soundly.

sentences.zh: 吾用韓休，為社稷耳，非為身也。」

translations.literal: My employing Han Xiu is for the altars of soil and grain—not for the person."
translations.idiomatic: I keep Han Xiu in office for the sake of the state, not for my own comfort."

sentences.zh: 有供奉侏儒名黃，性警黠。

translations.literal: There was a palace-attending dwarf named Huang, whose nature was alert and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: A dwarf named Huang served at court; he was quick-witted and sly.

sentences.zh: 上常憑之以行，謂之「肉幾」，寵賜甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor often leaned on him to walk, calling him "Flesh Stool," and favored and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor habitually leaned on him for support when walking, nicknamed him "Living Armrest," and showered him with gifts.

sentences.zh: 一日晚入，上怪之。

translations.literal: One day he entered late; the emperor wondered at it.
translations.idiomatic: One day he arrived late, and the emperor was puzzled.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣向入宮，道逢捕盜官與臣爭道，臣掀之墜馬，故晚。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject just now entering the palace, on the road met a bandit-catching official contending the road with your subject; your subject lifted him and he fell from his horse—therefore late."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "On my way to the palace I ran into a constable who tried to push me aside; I knocked him off his horse, which is why I am late."

sentences.zh: 因下階叩頭。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went down the steps and kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: He then descended the steps and kowtowed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「但使外無章奏，汝亦無憂。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Only if outside there are no memorials, you also need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So long as no report reaches me from outside, you have nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 有頃，京兆奏其狀。

translations.literal: Before long, the Metropolitan Prefecture memorialized the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later, the capital prefecture reported exactly what had happened.

sentences.zh: 上即叱出，付有司杖殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor at once shouted him out, handed him to the responsible office to beat to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately had him driven out and handed over to the authorities to be beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 閏月，癸酉，幽州道副總管郭英傑與契丹戰於都山，敗死。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on guiyou, Youzhou Circuit deputy commander Guo Yingjie fought the Khitan at Mount Du and was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on guiyou, Youzhou deputy commander Guo Yingjie battled the Khitan at Mount Du, was defeated, and killed.

sentences.zh: 時節度使薛楚玉遣英傑將精騎一萬及降奚擊契丹，屯於榆關之外。

translations.literal: At the time Military Commissioner Xue Chuyu sent Yingjie leading ten thousand elite cavalry and surrendered Xi to strike the Khitan, encamped outside Yuguan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Xue Chuyu had sent Yingjie with ten thousand elite horsemen and allied Xi tribes against the Khitan, camped beyond Yuguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 可突干引突厥之眾來合戰，奚持兩端，散走保險；

translations.literal: Ketugan led Turkish masses to join battle; the Xi held two ends, scattered and fled to secure passes;
translations.idiomatic: Ketugan brought Turkish forces to the fight while the Xi hedged their bets and melted away into the hills;

sentences.zh: 唐兵不利，英傑戰死。

translations.literal: Tang troops were unfavorable; Yingjie died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang force faltered and Yingjie fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 餘眾六千餘人猶力戰不已，虜以英傑首示之，竟不降，盡為虜所殺。

translations.literal: The remaining masses of more than six thousand still fought with force without ceasing; the barbarians used Yingjie's head to show them—they still did not surrender, and all were killed by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: More than six thousand survivors fought on; the enemy displayed Yingjie's head, yet they refused to yield and were slaughtered to the last man.

sentences.zh: 楚玉，訥之弟也。

translations.literal: Chuyu was Ne's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Chuyu was the younger brother of Xue Ne.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，癸亥，制：「自今選人有才業操行，委吏部臨時擢用；

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, on guihai, an edict: "From now on, for selected persons with talent, achievement, conduct, and character, entrust the Ministry of Personnel to promote and employ them at need;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, on guihai, an edict declared, "Henceforth candidates distinguished for ability and character may be promoted at the Ministry of Personnel's discretion;

sentences.zh: 流外奏用不復引過門下。」

translations.literal: Outsiders raised by memorial for employment need no longer pass through the Chancellery."
translations.idiomatic: appointees from outside the regular examination track need no longer be reviewed by the Chancellery."

sentences.zh: 雖有此制，而有司以循資格便於己，猶踵行之。

translations.literal: Although there was this statute, the responsible offices, because following seniority was convenient for themselves, still trod and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Despite the edict, officials continued the seniority system because it served their interests.

sentences.zh: 是時，官自三師以下一萬七千六百八十六員，吏自佐史以上五萬七千四百一十六員，而入仕之塗甚多，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: At this time, officials from the Three Preceptors downward numbered seventeen thousand six hundred eighty-six posts; clerks from assistant secretaries upward numbered fifty-seven thousand four hundred sixteen posts; and the paths of entering office were very many—impossible to enumerate completely.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were 17,686 official posts from the Three Preceptors down and 57,416 clerical posts from assistant secretary up, while routes into government service were so numerous they could not all be counted.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the yichou new moon, the sun had an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, at the yichou new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬午，立皇子沔為信王，泚為義王，漼為陳王，澄為豐王，潓為恆王，漎為梁王，滔為汴王。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renwu, the princes Min was made Prince of Xin, Ci Prince of Yi, Cui Prince of Chen, Cheng Prince of Feng, Hui Prince of Heng, Yong Prince of Liang, and Tao Prince of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renwu, the emperor ennobled his sons: Min as Prince of Xin, Ci as Prince of Yi, Cui as Prince of Chen, Cheng as Prince of Feng, Hui as Prince of Heng, Yong as Prince of Liang, and Tao as Prince of Bian.

sentences.zh: 關中久雨谷貴，上將幸東都，召京兆尹裴耀卿謀之，對曰：「關中帝業所興，當百代不易；

translations.literal: In Guanzhong, long rains made grain costly; the emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital and summoned Metropolitan Prefect Pei Yaojing to consult; he replied: "Guanzhong is where the imperial enterprise arose—it should be unchanged for a hundred generations;
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged rains had driven up grain prices in the Guanzhong region, and as the emperor prepared to move to Luoyang he summoned Pei Yaojing for counsel; Yaojing replied, "Guanzhong is the cradle of the dynasty and should remain the capital for ages to come;

sentences.zh: 但以地狹谷少，故乘輿時幸東都以寬之。

translations.literal: But because the land is narrow and grain few, therefore the imperial carriage occasionally visits the Eastern Capital to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: but its land is cramped and its harvests thin, so the court visits Luoyang from time to time to ease the strain.

sentences.zh: 臣聞貞觀、永徽之際，祿廩不多，歲漕關東一二十萬石，足以周贍，乘輿得以安居。

translations.literal: Your subject hears that at the border of Zhenguan and Yonghui, stipends and granaries were not many; yearly transport from east of the Pass of one or two hundred thousand shi was sufficient to complete provision, and the imperial carriage could thereby dwell in peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras, I am told, government stores were modest; shipping one or two hundred thousand shi annually from east of the Pass was enough to sustain the capital, and the court could remain at home.

sentences.zh: 今用度浸廣，運數倍於前，猶不能給，故使陛下數冒寒暑以恤西人。

translations.literal: Now expenditures gradually broaden; transport is several times that of before, yet still cannot supply—therefore causing Your Majesty repeatedly to brave cold and heat to show sympathy for western people.
translations.idiomatic: Today expenses have swollen and shipments have multiplied several times over, yet supplies still fall short—forcing Your Majesty to journey back and forth through summer heat and winter cold for the sake of the western populace.

sentences.zh: 今若使司農租米悉輸東都，自都轉漕，稍實關中，苟關中有數年之儲，則不憂水旱矣。

translations.literal: Now if one causes the Minister of Agriculture's rental rice all to be delivered to the Eastern Capital, and from the capital to transfer transport, gradually filling Guanzhong—if Guanzhong has several years' storage, then one need not worry about flood or drought.
translations.idiomatic: If all rent grain were sent first to Luoyang and then forwarded to the capital, Guanzhong's stores could gradually be replenished; with several years' reserves there, drought and flood would cease to be a concern.

sentences.zh: 且吳人不習河漕，所在停留，日月既久，遂生隱盜。

translations.literal: Moreover, Wu people are unaccustomed to river transport; wherever they stop, days and months being long, pilfering and theft then arise.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, southerners are unfamiliar with grain transport by river; long delays en route invite theft and embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 臣請於河口置倉，使吳船至彼即輸米而去，官自雇載分入河、洛。
