translations.literal: Your subject requests placing granaries at the river mouth, causing Wu boats on arrival there immediately to deliver rice and depart; the government itself hiring transport to distribute separately into the Yellow and Luo rivers.
translations.idiomatic: I propose building granaries at the river mouth where southern boats would unload and depart at once, with the state hiring carriers to move the grain up the Yellow and Luo rivers.

sentences.zh: 又於三門東西各置一倉，至者貯納，水險則止，水通則下，或開山路，車運而過，則無復留滯，省費巨萬矣。

translations.literal: Again, east and west of Sanmen each place one granary; those arriving store and accept—when water is dangerous then stop, when water opens then descend; or open mountain roads and cart transport to pass through—then there will be no further lingering delay, saving expense by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries should also be built east and west of Sanmen Pass to receive shipments: when the water is treacherous, cargo can wait; when it runs clear, boats can proceed—or goods can be hauled overland through mountain roads—eliminating delays and saving vast expense.

sentences.zh: 河、渭之濱，皆有漢、隋舊倉，葺之非難也。」

translations.literal: On the banks of the Yellow and Wei rivers, all have Han and Sui old granaries; repairing them is not difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Along the Yellow and Wei rivers stand granaries from Han and Sui times that could easily be restored."

sentences.zh: 上深然其言。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply persuaded.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚戌，上幸驪山溫泉；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on gengxu, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on gengxu, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 己未，還宮。

translations.literal: on jiwei he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on jiwei he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 戊子，左丞相宋璟致仕，歸東都。

translations.literal: On wuzi Left Chief Minister Song Jing retired from office and returned to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Left Chief Minister Song Jing retired and returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 韓休數與蕭嵩爭論於上前，面折嵩短，上頗不悅。

translations.literal: Han Xiu repeatedly debated with Xiao Song before the throne and openly exposed Song's faults; the emperor was rather displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu often argued with Xiao Song before the emperor and openly criticized him; the emperor grew displeased.

sentences.zh: 嵩因乞骸骨，上曰：「朕未厭卿，卿何為遽去！」

translations.literal: Song thereupon asked to retire; the emperor said: "I have not yet grown weary of you—why do you hurry to leave!"
translations.idiomatic: Song asked to retire; the emperor said, "I am not tired of you yet—why leave in such haste!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣蒙厚恩，待罪宰相，富貴已極，及陛下未厭臣，故臣得從容引去；

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant has received thick favor and, bearing guilt as chief minister, has reached the height of wealth and honor; while Your Majesty has not yet grown weary of me, I can therefore withdraw at ease;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I have enjoyed great favor and reached the peak of wealth as chief minister; while Your Majesty is not yet weary of me, I may still withdraw in peace;

sentences.zh: 君已厭臣，臣首領且不保，安能自遂！」

translations.literal: once the ruler has grown weary of his minister, the minister's head cannot even be preserved—how can he follow his own wish!"
translations.idiomatic: once a ruler tires of his minister, that minister cannot even keep his head—how could I do as I please!"

sentences.zh: 因泣下。

translations.literal: He thereupon wept.
translations.idiomatic: and he burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 上為之動容，曰：「卿且歸，朕徐思之。」

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and said: "Return for now; I shall think on it slowly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and said, "Go home for now; I will consider this carefully."

sentences.zh: 丁巳，嵩罷為左丞相，休罷為工部尚書。

translations.literal: On dingsi Song was removed and made Left Chief Minister; Han Xiu was removed and made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Song was demoted to Left Chief Minister and Han Xiu to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 以京兆尹裴耀卿為黃門侍郎，前中書侍郎張九齡時居母喪，起復中書侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: Pei Yaoqing, Intendant of Jingzhao, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; the former Vice Director Zhang Jiuling was then in mourning for his mother but was recalled to the same post; both were made Associate Chief Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaoqing, Intendant of Jingzhao, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; Zhang Jiuling, recalled from mourning for his mother, was also made Vice Director; both became Associate Chief Ministers.

sentences.zh: 是歲，分天下為京畿、都畿、關內、河南、河東、河北、隴右、山南東道、山南西道、劍南、淮南、江南東道、江南四道、黔中、嶺南，凡十五道，各置採訪使，以六條檢察非法；

translations.literal: That year the empire was divided into Jingji, Duji, Guannei, Henan, Hedong, Hebei, Longyou, Shannan East Circuit, Shannan West Circuit, Jiannan, Huainan, Jiangnan East Circuit, four Jiangnan circuits, Qianzhong, and Lingnan—fifteen circuits in all; each was given an Investigating Commissioner to inspect illegal acts by the Six Regulations;
translations.idiomatic: That year the empire was divided into fifteen circuits: Jingji, Duji, Guannei, Henan, Hedong, Hebei, Longyou, Shannan East, Shannan West, Jiannan, Huainan, Jiangnan East, the four Jiangnan circuits, Qianzhong, and Lingnan. Each received an investigating commissioner empowered under the six regulations to root out abuses;

sentences.zh: 兩畿以中丞領之，餘皆擇賢刺史領之。

translations.literal: the two capital districts were led by vice censors-in-chief; the rest were all led by selected worthy prefects.
translations.idiomatic: the two metropolitan districts were headed by vice censors-in-chief; elsewhere worthy prefects were chosen to lead them.

sentences.zh: 非官有遷免，則使無廢更。

translations.literal: unless the official was transferred or dismissed, the commissioner was not replaced.
translations.idiomatic: commissioners were not replaced unless their nominal post changed.

sentences.zh: 惟變革舊章，乃須報可；

translations.literal: only when altering old statutes was approval required;
translations.idiomatic: only changes to established rules required prior approval;

sentences.zh: 自餘聽便宜從事，先行後聞。

translations.literal: for the rest they were permitted to act as circumstances required, acting first and reporting afterward.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise they could act on their own authority and report afterward.

sentences.zh: 太府卿楊崇禮，政道之子也，在太府二十餘年，前後為太府者莫能及。

translations.literal: Grand Steward Yang Chongli was a son of Zhengdao; he served in the Grand Steward's office more than twenty years, and none who held the post before or after could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Steward Yang Chongli, son of Zhengdao, served in that office for more than twenty years; none of his predecessors or successors matched him.

sentences.zh: 時承平日久，財貨山積，嘗經楊卿者，無不精美；

translations.literal: The age had been long at peace; wealth piled like mountains; whatever had passed through Steward Yang was without exception refined;
translations.idiomatic: Peace had lasted so long that wealth piled up like mountains; everything that passed through Yang's hands was impeccably managed;

sentences.zh: 每歲句駁省便，出錢數百萬緡。

translations.literal: each year at the seasonal audit he saved convenience and disbursed several million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: each year his audits saved the treasury millions of strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以戶部尚書致仕，年九十餘矣。

translations.literal: That year he retired as Minister of Revenue at more than ninety years of age.
translations.idiomatic: That year he retired as Minister of Revenue at over ninety.

sentences.zh: 上問宰相：「崇禮諸子，誰能繼其父者？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chief ministers: "Among Chongli's sons, who can succeed his father?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the chief ministers, "Which of Chongli's sons can succeed him?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「崇禮三子，慎餘、慎矜、慎名，皆廉勤有才，而慎矜為優。」

translations.literal: They replied: "Chongli has three sons—Shenyu, Shenjin, and Shenming—all frugal, diligent, and talented, but Shenjin is the best."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "His three sons Shenyu, Shenjin, and Shenming are all capable and diligent, but Shenjin is the finest."

sentences.zh: 上乃擢慎矜自汝陽令為監察御史，知太府出納，慎名攝監察御史，知含嘉倉出給，亦皆稱職；

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon promoted Shenjin from magistrate of Ruyang to investigating censor, in charge of receipts and disbursements at the Grand Steward's office; Shenming was made acting investigating censor, in charge of issues from the Hejia granary; both likewise performed their duties well;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promoted Shenjin from magistrate of Ruyang to investigating censor overseeing the Grand Steward's treasury, and made Shenming acting censor over the Hejia granary; both proved capable;

sentences.zh: 上甚悅之。

translations.literal: the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 慎矜奏諸州所輸布帛有漬污穿破者，皆下本州征折估錢，轉市輕貨，徵調始繁矣。

translations.literal: Shenjin memorialized that wherever cloth and silk submitted by the prefectures were stained or torn, the home prefecture should be ordered to collect compensatory valuation money and convert it to purchase light goods—from this requisitions began to grow burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjin proposed that stained or torn tribute cloth be charged back to the submitting prefecture at a discount, with the shortfall made up in light goods—and from this tax collection grew ever more burdensome.
